title: Lathe chuck collision solid: bore wall is drawn up to 0.12 % short of the true bore, and the envelope test tolerates a 0.5 mm shrink

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:turning
labels.description: Lathe and mill-turn

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Found by the review of PR 1469 (lathe chuck fixtures as collision geometry).

What happens: the chuck's round outer faces are drawn with flats placed 0.12 % outside the true circle, so the collision solid never falls inside the real part. The bore wall is drawn the other way round: its flats leave the wall up to 0.12 % of the bore radius short of the true bore (0.012 mm on a 20 mm collet bore), so the modelled chuck has slightly less material there than the real one. The code comment at that place claims the opposite (that the bore is conservative).

A second gap: the sim test that pins the envelope probes points 0.5 to 1 mm from the rim and the jaw tip, so a solid shrunk by less than 0.5 mm there would still pass.

Expected: every face of a fixture's collision solid is on or outside the real surface (for a bore: on or inside the true bore radius), the comment says what the code does, and the test pins the envelope to the tessellation allowance, not to half a millimetre.

Done means: the bore polygon is inscribed in the true bore (or the allowance is applied inward), the comment is corrected, and the envelope test probes within the stated allowance of the rim, jaw tip and bore wall and fails on a solid shrunk by more than it.

Applies once PR 1469 is on main (the code is not on main before the next cut).

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Found by the review of PR 1464 (the kernel-side `.sc` reader, part of issue 1456).

What is missing:
- NaN or huge coordinates in a `.sc` body are not refused in the Solidcraft reader itself; it relies on the shared STEP-side checks, and no test feeds such a body through `import_solidcraft`.
- The fuzz-style test `damaged_files_never_panic_or_hang` damages bytes of the container, so almost every copy stops at the CRC-32 check and the body decoder (where a hang or an oversized allocation could live) is barely reached.

Wanted:
- A test that builds a `.sc` with a valid container and checksum around a body carrying NaN, infinite and out-of-range coordinates, and asserts a named refusal.
- A fuzz-style test that damages the decompressed body and re-wraps it with a correct CRC, so the decoder itself is exercised; with a time bound so a hang fails the test.

This is an importer of untrusted files (Prime Directive: corrupt models give a clean error, never a crash or hang). It must land before the reader is wired into the app or MCP.

Done means: both tests exist in `crates/kernel/tests/` and pass; any defect they show is fixed in the reader with a named error.

title: Machining mesh refuses the Solidcraft sample body at every chord (deviation ~2.8x the tolerance)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Found while working #1456 (Solidcraft `.sc` import, kernel side).

The final body of the maintainer's sample design (`testdata/models/solidcraft_for_beginners.sc`, added on the #1456 branch) imports through `camcraft_kernel::solidcraft::import_solidcraft` as a checked solid (volume > 0, the port's box is exactly the design's [-62.5, 62.5] x [-62.5, 62.5] x [0, 85] mm). But `camcraft_kernel::machining_mesh::machining_mesh` refuses it at every chord tried, always by the deviation verdict:

| chord (mm) | refusal |
|---|---|
| 0.005 | face 50 stands 6.847e-3 mm off its surface |
| 0.01 | face 1 stands 2.348e-2 mm off its surface |
| 0.02 | face 36 stands 6.146e-2 mm off its surface |
| 0.05 | face 36 stands 1.337e-1 mm off its surface |
| 0.1 | face 36 stands 2.820e-1 mm off its surface |

The measured deviation grows with the chord at about 2.8x it, so the planner is not honouring the tolerance on some faces of this body (blends and a tilted cut plane: features 12-19 of the design). The refusal is the right outcome (Prime Directive), but it means the body cannot be machined once the app is wired to the import.

Reproduce: on the #1456 branch, import the sample with `import_solidcraft` and call `machining_mesh(&solid, tol, &CancelToken::new())`.

Done means: the sample's final body meshes at the app chord (0.005 mm) inside tolerance, or the faces that cannot are named with why, pinned by a test on the sample.

Related: #1029 (crafted records for every solidcore-tess shortfall), #940.

title: Import a DXF drawing and use its profiles as geometry for 2D cuts

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "We should be able to load DXF file to do profile cuts on."

What is missing: the importers read solid and mesh models only. A 2D drawing (a DXF from a CAD or sheet-metal program) cannot be loaded, so a flat part cannot be profiled without first being modelled as a solid. No DXF code exists in the tree today; issues 743 and 744 want DXF for tool and fixture profiles and can share this reader.

Wanted:
- A DXF reader for the 2D entities that carry a profile: LINE, ARC, CIRCLE, LWPOLYLINE and POLYLINE (with bulges), ELLIPSE and SPLINE (flattened within a tolerance, arcs kept as arcs where they are arcs). Units from `$INSUNITS`, with a question to the user when the file states none (never a silent guess between mm and inch). Layers are kept, so the user can pick by layer. Blocks/INSERT are expanded or refused by name; text, dimensions and hatches are skipped and counted in the import summary.
- The drawing loads as sketch geometry on the setup's XY plane: shown in the viewport, placed with the stock, saved in the project file.
- Chaining: touching entities are joined into chains within a tolerance; closed chains are told from open ones, and outer loops from holes.
- The 2D operations (2D Contour first; Pocket, Slot, Engrave and the plasma/laser profile operations after) take those chains as their geometry selection, with side (inside/outside) and direction per chain, exactly as they take model edges today.
- Loading is an undoable command with its MCP tool (Everything Is a Command; commands ship with an MCP tool). Model > Open offers `.dxf`, and so does the viewport drop of issue 1450.

Safety:
- The reader is an importer of untrusted files: malformed group codes, truncated files, NaN or huge coordinates, zero-length entities and self-intersecting loops give a clean error or a named skip, never a crash or a hang; it gets a fuzz test like the other importers.
- A gap wider than the chaining tolerance leaves an open chain that is shown as open; it is never closed silently, and an inside/outside cut on an open chain is refused by name.
- A flattened spline or ellipse stays within the stated tolerance of the drawn curve, pinned by a test, so the cut part is to size.
- Units are part of the result: the import summary states them, and a wrong-unit part (25.4 times too big or small) cannot happen without the user having answered the question.

Sources: the DXF format from Autodesk's published DXF reference (a public file-format document; format only), written from scratch or through a permissively licensed crate if one fits (a new dependency needs the maintainer's yes and a `docs/decisions/` entry). No DXF sample files taken from another product's install tree.

Scope note: this is larger than one PR. Suggested split when it is picked up: (1) reader + fuzz test in the geometry crate, (2) sketch entity, project file and viewport display, (3) chaining and selection in 2D Contour, (4) the other 2D operations.

Done means: a DXF with an outer rectangle, two circles and a slot made of lines and arcs loads, shows in the viewport and survives save/reopen; a 2D Contour picks the outer loop (outside) and the holes (inside) and posts a program whose golden CL matches the drawn sizes; a file with no units asks; an open chain is shown and refused for a side-compensated cut; a corrupt DXF gives a named error; the fuzz test runs; undo removes the drawing; the MCP tool loads a DXF headlessly.

title: Post-merge test: run the batch gate on the self-hosted Linux runner on every push to main

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Asked for by the user (2026-11-13, in chat): "Can we setup a build test post merge using local gh runner?"

## Why

AGENTS.md "Fixes are tested in the background" has the main session dispatch a gate-runner agent to run the batch tier on `origin/main` after a fix merges, in the shared main checkout. That costs agent tokens. It blocks the main checkout and any cut meanwhile. It's skipped when a session is busy, so several PRs that were each tested alone merge untested together: today #1432, #1165 and #1181 merged in one batch, after #1405, #1397, #1421 and #1436. The self-hosted Linux runner from #1413 / PR #1418 can run this for free.

## What

A workflow, e.g. `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml`:
- **Trigger:** `push` to `main` only, plus `workflow_dispatch` (input: ref). This is the "user's say-so" AGENTS.md requires for a `push` trigger. Only merged, reviewed code reaches `main`, so no fork can run code on the runner. Never `pull_request` or `pull_request_target`.
- **Runner:** `runs-on: [self-hosted, linux]` (0 billed minutes).
- **Concurrency:** one group for `main` with `cancel-in-progress: true`, so a burst of merges tests only the newest head. The runner is also the cut runner; a cut must not be starved, so say how they share it (e.g. the cut's jobs take priority, or post-merge yields while a `release/*` cut is running).
- **Gate:** `cargo xtask gate batch` (no release-mode heavy lanes; target ≤ 20 min), wrapped in `xvfb-run -a` for the UI suites. Always upload `gate-logs/` as an artifact.
- **On red:** the run fails visibly. Decide how agents and the maintainer hear about it: e.g. the job comments on, or opens, one rolling `main is red` issue (P1, or P0 when it's a G-code test) naming the failing suites and the commit range, and closes it on the next green run. Keep it to one issue, not one per run.
- **Permissions:** `contents: read`, and `issues: write` only on the reporting step.

## Also changes

AGENTS.md "Fixes are tested in the background" (the workflow replaces the gate-runner dispatch; the local batch stays the fallback when the runner is down), and "GitHub Actions minutes are budgeted" (a `push` trigger on `main` to the self-hosted runner only). It's a process change, so it bumps `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` and gets announced on #681. A `.github` change gets `needs-maintainer`.

Builds on #1413 (PR #1418, the self-hosted runner and its AGENTS.md section): stack on it, or wait for it to merge.

Done means: a merge to `main` starts the batch gate on the self-hosted runner without anyone dispatching it; a red run tells the agents (the rolling issue); a green run closes that issue; bursts of merges test only the newest head; a cut is never blocked by it; and AGENTS.md says so.

title: Operations: pre-drilled holes as entry positions (plunge to full depth instead of helix)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "Another issue is setting pre drilled holes as starting points for some operations so we can dive down and do properly full depth cuts instead of trying to helix down little bit at a time..."

What is missing: a pocket or adaptive operation in closed material always works its own way down (helix or ramp), a little at a time. The usual shop method, drilling a start hole first and plunging the end mill down it to full depth, cannot be set up: the operation does not know a hole is there.

Wanted: on 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive, Slot and the 3D roughing operations, an "Entry positions (pre-drilled)" group:
- Pick one or more points or existing drilled holes (a drilling operation earlier in the setup, a hole in the model, or a typed point with a diameter and depth).
- At such a position the tool goes straight down the hole at the plunge/rapid-in-clearance feed to the cutting depth and starts the full-depth cut from there, with no helix or ramp. Depth passes may then be full depth (the user's stepdown still rules).
- Regions with no entry position keep the helix or ramp, or are refused if the user chose "pre-drilled only".

Safety (this is a plunge into what the program believes is air):
- The hole must really be there when the operation runs: its source is an earlier operation in the same setup (or carried stock from a previous setup), checked against the stock simulation; a typed point with no drilling behind it is allowed only with the user's explicit "the hole exists" choice, shown in the operation summary and the setup sheet.
- The hole must be at least as wide as the tool plus a clearance and at least as deep as the plunge; otherwise refused by name with the numbers. A hole with a drill-point cone is counted only to its full-diameter depth.
- The entry must lie inside the region to cut, and the first sideways move starts from the hole wall, not from solid.
- The rapid-in-stock and gouge checks stay on: a plunge down a hole that the simulation does not show is refused at the post like any other.

Related: the companion issue on user-set start and exit points (filed with this one); tool kinds for drills are issue 897.

Done means: a closed pocket with a drilled start hole from an earlier operation plunges down the hole and cuts at full depth with no helix (golden CL, simulation clean); a hole too small or too shallow is refused by name in tests; a typed position without a drilling operation is refused unless the explicit choice is set; undo and redo; MCP parameters; the structural UI test covers the group.

title: Operations: user-set start and exit points, path regenerated to them

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: area:ui

labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "we should be able to set start points on generated path and also exit points.. So the path gets regenerated to those."

What is missing: where an operation starts cutting and where it leaves is chosen by the generator alone. The user cannot say "enter here" or "leave here", for example to keep the entry mark off a visible face, to start a contour away from a clamp, or to end next to the following feature.

Wanted: on the operations where it has a meaning (2D Contour, Pocket, Adaptive, Face, Slot, Bore, and the 3D finishing passes that have a free start), two optional picks:
- Start point(s): picked in the viewport (a point on the model, a sketch point or typed coordinates). For a closed contour the path is re-sequenced to begin at the pick's nearest point on the chain, with its lead-in there; for a pocket or adaptive region the entry (helix, ramp or plunge) is placed at the pick. One pick per chain or region; chains with no pick keep the automatic choice.
- Exit point(s): the same for where the pass ends and the lead-out is placed.

Changing a pick is an undoable command (it edits the operation parameters) and regenerates the path. MCP: the same parameters on the operation tools.

Safety: a pick is a wish, never an override of a check. If the entry, lead or ramp at the picked place does not fit (helix does not fit in the region, lead-in gouges a wall, the point is outside the machinable region or inside a keep-out or fixture), the operation is refused by name or marked incomplete, saying which pick and why; it never moves the entry silently and never posts a path that the collision or gouge checks would refuse at the automatic entry.

Related: the companion issue on pre-drilled holes as entry positions (filed with this one).

Done means: a closed 2D contour with a picked start begins and leads in at that point and, with a picked exit, leads out there (golden CL); a pocket enters at its picked point; an impossible pick is refused by name in a test; undo and redo restore the previous path; the MCP tools take the picks; the structural UI test covers the two pick rows.

On sources: "We should use perplexity to find literature on those types of toolpaths and not copy them straight up".

What is missing: plasma/laser nesting cuts every part as its own closed profile with its own pierce and leads. Parts with a shared straight edge cannot be cut with one pass along that edge (common-line cutting), and there is no "mark before cut" ordering.

Wanted:
- Common-line cutting: in a nest, two parts placed one kerf width apart along a straight edge are cut with a single pass there. The paths of both parts are re-ordered so the shared edge is cut once and no part drops before its remaining edges are cut. A user option on the nest (off by default), with the kerf from the tool.
- Marking first: operations flagged as marking (low-power scribe or engrave) run before any cutting on the sheet.

Safety: a part must not be cut free while a later pass still has to run on it or start from it (a tipped part is a torch collision). The shared pass must leave both parts to size (kerf centred on the gap). Pierces stay off the part outline. Refuse by name when the gap is not one kerf wide or the shared edges are not parallel.

Sources: step one of the work is a literature search (Perplexity) for published material on common-line cutting and cut sequencing for sheet nests; the code is written from that and named in the provenance comment. camlib is a feature list only: no code is copied or adapted from it.

Done means: two rectangles nested with a shared edge post one pass on that edge and one pierce fewer; both parts measure to size in the path check; the cut-order test proves no part is free before its last pass; golden .nc for the plasma post; MCP option; the literature used is cited in the PR.

Sources: step one of the work is a literature search (Perplexity) for published material on undercut and T-slot milling paths and on simulating non-convex tool profiles (tri-dexel or equivalent); the code is written from those and named in the provenance comment. camlib is a feature list only: no code is copied or adapted from it.

What is there today: the built-in fixture library generates milling workholding from parameters - vises (#788, #787, #820), grid/dowel plates (#819) and accessories (#789). A lathe setup has no generated workholding body: a chuck is only there if the user imports one (STEP/DXF, #744 is the open import work), and the workholding max rpm (#1031) and the holder-against-jaws check (#1037) have nothing built in to work on.

- Collet chuck: nose diameter and length, collet bore set from the stock diameter, nose stick-out.

Each one:
- is created by an undoable command with its MCP tool (AGENTS.md "Commands ship with an MCP tool"), and placed on the spindle axis of a turning setup with "Fit to the stock";
- is a fixture body like the vises: shown in the viewport and simulation, and judged by the existing turning collision checks (holder and insert against the jaws, #1037) - a generated chuck must never be skipped by a check that an imported one gets;
- carries its max rpm into the setup's workholding limit (#1031) when the user enters one;
- is refused by name in a milling setup unless it sits on a rotary axis (a 4th-axis chuck is #821's neighbourhood; out of scope here unless it falls out for free).

Related: #744 (fixtures as spun bodies, import), #339 (umbrella: handle fixtures/vises), #832, #821.

Done means: the Fixtures page offers "3-jaw chuck", "4-jaw chuck" and "Collet chuck" for a turning setup; each is generated from its parameters, fits to the stock, undoes and redoes, has an MCP tool, and a turning pass that would run the holder into a generated jaw is refused exactly like with an imported chuck (pinned by tests, one per chuck type for generation and one for the collision refusal).

title: Doosan DNM 5700: the optional A states no nose_to_axis, so the index-swing law refuses every program on the built-in, even plain 3-axis work at A0

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

Found while fixing #1410. With the DNM travel stated per the travel rule, a plate contour at A0 passes the stroke check, but the post gate still refuses it:

```
2D Contour1: Doosan DNM 5700 turns the work on A but states no nose_to_axis - the tool's clearance over the part swept by the A0.000 index cannot be judged
```

`assets/machines/doosan-dnm.mch` declares the catalog's *optional* 4th-axis table (`rot_a`) with no `nose_to_axis`, so `index_swing_problems` (`crates/app/src/posting_index_swing.rs`) refuses every op on this machine. No program posts on the built-in DNM 5700.

## Workaround

State the setup's own `nose_to_axis` (`SetSetupNoseToAxis` / MCP `set_setup_nose_to_axis`), or use another machine.

## Options (pick one; no figure may be invented)

1. State a real `nose_to_axis` for the DNM's rotary, from a published figure for the rotary table the catalog names.
2. Split the file: a plain 3-axis DNM 5700 (no A) and a DNM 5700 + rotary table that carries the figure, or keeps refusing until it is stated.
3. Do not refuse an op whose path never leaves the program's start A when no index happens. This is a change to a safety law, and needs the maintainer.

Done means: a 3-axis face job on a built-in DNM 5700 machine posts, and the rotary variant still refuses an unjudgeable index by name. Pinned in `crates/app/tests/vmc_stroke.rs` (`a_plate_contour_on_the_built_in_dnm_passes_the_stroke` currently asserts that this is the only refusal).

title: Process: a P1/P2 issue filed after a cut has started does not restart the cut

labels.name: area:build

labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat, after the v0.19.0 cut): "We should as a rule not let P1/P2s coming in after cut - force a restart as its a ~2 hour job".

## What happened

AGENTS.md says "A minor/major cut does not start while any `P1` or `P2` issue is open". During the v0.19.0 cut two such issues were filed after the release branch existed (issue 1417, P1, a red xtask unit test; issue 1398, P2, the Fanuc lathe live-tool feed cap). Fixing them in the cut means merging to main, merging main into the release branch and running the release gate again, about 50 minutes of gate and about two hours in all. The maintainer decided in the question dialog: "Tag now as it is"; both were named as known issues on the release PR.

## What to change (AGENTS.md, "Priorities" and "Commits and Releases")

- The `P1`/`P2` rule is a start condition: it is checked once, when the cut starts (step 1). The session records the time and the list of open `P1`/`P2` issues (none) in the release PR body.
- A `P1` or `P2` issue filed after that moment does not restart the cut and is not merged into it. The cut finishes on the tree that passed the release gate. Each such issue is named under "Known issues" in the release notes on the GitHub release and in a comment on the release PR, and its fix merges after the tag and ships in the next minor.
- The maintainer can still stop a cut by saying so; no agent stops or restarts one for a late issue. An agent that finds a late `P1` (unsafe or wrong output) tells the maintainer in one line and goes on.
- Failures of the cut's own release gate are different: they are what the gate is for, and are still fixed in the cut as today.
- Update the `merge-ready` skill's precondition text and the release steps where they repeat the rule.

Process files change: bump `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`, add a `docs/decisions/` entry quoting the maintainer, announce on issue 681 when it merges.

title: Agent coordination broker: leases, heartbeats and dispatch across concurrent agents (coor CLI + Cloudflare Worker)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: needs-research
labels.description: Large idea with open questions: research and file sub-issues before any code

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
A proposal from a contributor (relayed by the user, 2026-11-13), with M5's assessment. Filed as research: open design questions to answer and break into sub-issues before any code.

## Problem

Several concurrent agents (Claude sessions on different subscriptions and machines, Codex, human contributors) work this repo. Today they coordinate only through GitHub text conventions:
- claim comments, re-read 60 s later for races;
- the 4 h agent and 48 h contributor staleness rules;
- `in-review`, `conflicts` and `merge-ready` labels;
- review markers;
- a review lock that is a local file on one machine;
- across subscriptions, messages are relayed by hand by the user.

The results are clashing PRs, stale claims, duplicated work (e.g. #1377 / #1379), and a human in the loop for every cross-account message.

## Proposal (contributor's, summarised)

- **A `coor` CLI exposed to agents as a skill**, configured by `.env` (channel, broker endpoint, agent id, token):
  - `coor lock <issue|module>`: take a lease;
  - `coor status`: heartbeat, plus current leases;
  - `coor next`: get the highest-priority unleased work order;
  - `coor dispatch`: report a finished unit.
- **A broker on Cloudflare Workers** with Durable Objects holding the lease table and session registry. Leases auto-expire on missed heartbeats, and the broker flags stale branches.
- **GitHub webhooks** feed new issues and PRs to a maintenance/dispatcher agent, which turns them into work orders.
- The original suggests **ZeroMQ compiled to WASM** as the transport.

## Assessment (M5)

**Keep:**
- leases with a heartbeat TTL;
- a small CLI as a skill (works for non-Claude agents too, no MCP server needed);
- a dispatcher (`coor next`);
- webhook ingestion instead of polling.

**Change:**
- **Transport.** Cloudflare Workers can't accept inbound raw TCP (`connect()` is outbound only), so a `tcp://...workers.dev:5555` ZMQ endpoint can't work. One Durable Object per project plus HTTP and WebSocket gives the consistency and notifications without ZMQ or a WASM port.
- **Lease granularity.** Lease the issue and declare the modules it touches, and warn on overlap; don't lock files. The real collisions are on shared hot files (`lib.rs`, `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`, `assets/posts/*.cps`, `CHANGELOG.md`), and file locks there would serialize everyone. This automates AGENTS.md's "an issue touching code an open PR changes stacks/waits".
- **Unlocks.** Don't rely on SIGINT unlocks. Agent sessions end without clean exits (compaction, API errors, reboots); the heartbeat TTL is the mechanism, and an explicit unlock is a bonus.
- **GitHub stays the record.** The broker mirrors each lease to the existing claim comment and label, so forks, humans and agents outside the system still see it, and nothing breaks if the broker is down.
- **A message channel between agents** (addressed lines, e.g. `@SKULL: #1181 head X ready for re-review`) rides the same broker. That removes the user from the relay loop.

## Open questions

1. **Identity and auth.** One token per agent, issued how? Should agents also get separate GitHub identities (machine users or a GitHub App), since everyone posts as one account today and claims are told apart by text?
2. **Lease scope.** Issue plus declared modules, with an overlap warning or a refusal? How are the "modules it touches" declared, and how are they checked against the PR's actual diff?
3. **Staleness.** The TTL per lease kind (work, review, research), and how it maps onto AGENTS.md's 4 h and 48 h rules. Does the broker replace those rules or only enforce them?
4. **The dispatcher.** Does it only order by P, lanes and effort (deterministic), or is it an agent that also splits issues? Does it know each subscription's remaining budget?
5. **Mirroring to GitHub.** Which token posts the mirror comments, and how are drift or a broker outage reconciled?
6. **Hosting and cost.** Cloudflare free tier (Workers plus Durable Objects) vs. a small VM; who owns the account and its secrets.
7. **The fork case.** How a fork's agents join: the channel is per project, so do fork contributors get read-only or full leases?
8. **The cheaper interim.** A pinned "coordination" issue that every agent reads and posts to each tick, as an hour-long first step. Is it worth doing while this is designed?
9. **Process.** The AGENTS.md changes (claim rules, Pick, lanes) and the PROCESS_VERSION bump once it ships.

## Done means

Every open question above is answered in comments here. The concrete sub-issues are filed: at minimum the broker, the CLI and skill, GitHub mirroring, the webhook ingest, and the AGENTS.md process change. Each carries one `P*`, one `effort:*`, `area:*`, `source:agent`, a "Done means" line and "Part of #<this>". Then this umbrella is closed.

title: PR test pipeline on the self-hosted runner: the PR-reviewer hands the build and tests to GitHub Actions when a runner is online

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "there should be an agent change and prob pr-reviewer change that when the pr-review is done instead of doing the build locally, we check if there is hosted github runners present and push the testing as PR build to the github actions self hosted runner... Which means prob both the pr-reviewer skill need or just the skill need to be able to determine that and the testing pipeline needs to be created."

Related: issue 1413 (cut pipeline, Linux, self-hosted runners only), issue 1415 / PR 1416 (removes the unused `ci.yml` and `nightly.yml`).

## Why

Every PR review builds the workspace and runs the touched suites in a worktree on the reviewer's machine: 10-20 GB of `target/` each, up to four at once, competing with gates and cuts for the same machine.

## What

1. **A PR test workflow** (here `pr-test.yml`) for the self-hosted Linux runner (`runs-on: [self-hosted, linux]`): input is a PR number; it trial-merges the PR head with current main, builds, runs `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (the suites the diff touches) and clippy for the touched crates, and reports pass/fail per binary with the failing output.
2. **Runner detection.** Before building, the reviewer asks whether a self-hosted runner is online (`gh api repos/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runners --jq '.runners[] | select(.status=="online")'`). Online: start the workflow for the PR (`gh workflow run pr-test.yml -f pr=<N>`), wait for the run (`gh run watch`), and read its result and logs into the review. None online, or the run cannot start: build locally as today. The review comment says which of the two ran, with the run's link.
3. **Where the logic lives.** In the `review-prs` skill and the `PR-reviewer` agent definition (`.claude/agents/PR-reviewer.md`); decide whether detection sits in the skill (the dispatcher starts the run, the reviewer reads it) or in the agent. The reviewer still reads the diff, checks AGENTS.md's laws and writes the review itself; only the build and test step moves.

## Open questions (decide before code)

- **Trigger and safety.** A self-hosted runner executes the PR's code (build scripts, tests) on the maintainer's hardware. AGENTS.md says "Never add a `push`, `pull_request` or `schedule` trigger without the user's say-so". Proposed: `workflow_dispatch` only, started by a collaborator's session, so a fork PR can never start a run by itself; the job gets no secrets and a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`; the runner works in a clean checkout per run. A `pull_request` trigger for PRs from collaborators' own branches is the alternative, and needs the maintainer's explicit yes.
- **`needs-maintainer` PRs.** Today a PR with a new dependency or a `build.rs` / scripts / `.github` change is read, not built. That rule should hold on the runner too.
- **Linux only.** Windows-only readings (per-OS pinned values, the Windows arm of issue 1402) are not checked by a Linux run; say whether the reviewer still runs those locally when the diff touches them.
- **Concurrency.** One runner, up to four reviews: a queue (`concurrency:` per PR), and what the reviewer does while it waits.
- **UI tests.** The ui suites spawn the real app through the test harness; say whether the runner can run them headless or they stay local.
- **Fallback truthfulness.** A run that is cancelled or times out is not a pass: the reviewer falls back to the local build or reports "not built".

## Also changes

`.claude/agents/PR-reviewer.md`, `.claude/skills/review-prs/SKILL.md` and AGENTS.md ("Outside PRs are reviewed", "GitHub Actions minutes are budgeted") are process files: the PR bumps `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` and is announced on issue 681. A `.github` change is read by the maintainer before it merges.

Done means: with the runner online, a review of a test PR starts the workflow, the review comment carries the run's link and per-binary result, and no local build ran; with the runner offline, the same review builds locally as today; a fork PR cannot start the workflow by itself; AGENTS.md and the runner setup notes describe it.

title: Process: the PR review compares 3-5 named risk spots against their reference instead of sampling; a PR sent back twice escalates its effort tier

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
**What happens.** The `PR-reviewer` checks a PR against the laws (unwrap, commands, layering, placement, process) and runs the touched suites, but nothing tells it *where* a behaviour bug is most likely or what to compare the new code with. With a large diff it ends up sampling. And there is no bound on review rounds: a PR can go `needs-rework` -> fix -> full review -> `needs-rework` again, each round on the same (possibly too cheap) worker tier and each round a full review build.

**Evidence.** In another agent-driven Rust project of this contributor, run with the same builder -> reviewer setup, an evaluation on 2026-11-12 found that reviews without named spots took samples and found nothing; the one real finding of the period came only when the dispatcher named the risky places and the reference function to compare with. The same project caps the loop at one rework per tier.

**Proposal (process files only):**
1. `work-issue` step 5: the draft PR body carries a `Risk spots:` list - 3-5 entries, each `file:function - what could go wrong - reference` (the issue's Done means, the public source in the module's provenance line, or the existing function / law the change mirrors). Typical spots: new geometry or formulas, anything that reaches posted G-code, file/project writing and round-trip, state across frames, undo/redo and abort paths.
2. `PR-reviewer` step 5: a new first item "Risk spots, not samples": take the PR's list (or choose 3-5 itself when it is missing), read each hunk and its reference, compare step by step, and name in the review what each spot was compared with.
3. AGENTS.md "Escalation, never silent" and `work-issue` step 4: a PR whose second full review is again `needs-rework` is not reworked a third time on the same tier - the issue's effort label rises one step and the next rework goes to that tier (`max`: `blocked`, maintainer decides).
4. `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` +1.

Suggested labels: `P5`, `effort:low`, `source:agent` (the contributor cannot set labels).

**Done means:** the four files carry the rules above; a fork that syncs to the new PROCESS_VERSION gets them; #681 has the announcement line when it merges.

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "We need an issue for a "Cut" pipeline on Github Actions that will be building and testing the cut on github rather than locally. And when that is done it will run the Release pipeline for that tagged version."

## Why

The v0.19.0 cut ran the release gate tier locally in the main checkout: about 75 minutes per run, three runs (two red, one after the fixes), with the checkout and the machine blocked for every other session meanwhile. Suites that only run in the release tier (kernel STEP agreement, the app heavy lane, the UI snapshot lane) went red only at the cut.

## What

A manually started workflow (`workflow_dispatch`, input: the version), here called `cut.yml`, that takes a `release/vX.Y.0` branch and:

1. builds it and runs the release gate tier on GitHub (`cargo xtask gate release`, or the same lanes split into jobs);
2. on green, makes the cut's tag on the release merge commit and starts the existing release pipeline (`release.yml`) for that tag; on red, tags nothing and reports the failing lanes.

## Open questions (decide before code)

- **Actions budget.** AGENTS.md budgets 3000 minutes a month, Windows billed 2x, macOS 10x, and says "Never add a `push`, `pull_request` or `schedule` trigger without the user's say-so". The local release gate is about 75 minutes on a warm cache; a cold Windows runner will be slower and bills double. Which OS runs the gate (Linux only, or Windows too because the pinned move counts differ per OS, issue 1402)? What caching (sccache, `Swatinem/rust-cache`)?
- **Where the tag is made.** Today step 4 tags the release PR's merge commit by hand after `git diff $tip $m` is empty. Does the workflow run before the release PR merges (on the branch) and tag after the merge, or run on main after the merge? A tag pushed with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` does not trigger `release.yml`; the workflow has to call it (`workflow_call`) or use another token.
- **Snapshot goldens.** They are regenerated at the cut after a human look at the `.diff.png` files. The workflow needs to hand those files over (artifact upload) and wait, or the regeneration stays a local step before the workflow starts.
- **Version bump, zip and installer.** `cargo xtask release --no-tag --installer` does these locally today; `release.yml` builds the published artifact. Say which of them move.
- **What stays local.** The quick and batch tiers are not part of this issue.

## Also changes

AGENTS.md "Commits and Releases" (the cut steps) and "GitHub Actions minutes are budgeted" describe the local cut; a PR for this changes them, bumps `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` and is announced on the pinned issue 681. A `.github` change is read by the maintainer before it merges (`needs-maintainer`).

Done means: a cut of a test version on a scratch branch runs the gate on GitHub from one manual start, a red gate makes no tag, a green one ends with the release pipeline's artifact attached to the GitHub release for that tag, and AGENTS.md describes the new steps with the billed minutes of one cut measured and written down.

title: Land model: stepped lids churn a retract-and-plunge at every lid step edge

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## The churn, root-caused

Follow-up to #1286 (the land model), picking up the finding from my review of that PR: on a part whose surface is not flat, the path fragments around the lids — every crossing of a filled hole costs a retract → rapid → plunge every ~0.5–1 mm instead of one continuous lateral bridge.

The cause is downstream of the fill rule itself: **the closing levels a lid's cells a hair apart, and `emit` gives each cell its own height, so the lid is a staircase.** At each step edge the ball can seat on neither plane for a full ball-width annulus — the higher lid top blocks it from seating on the lower, and a lid top's free edge carries no fold support (lids are horizontal tops-only quads). Support goes `None` across that annulus, and the march retracts and plunges at every step.

Repro: the #1196 part (4B52391, two stepped through-holes, roof descending ~0.04 mm per 1.06 mm grid cell across hole 1). `fill_openings(width = 12.7, tol = 0.01)`, then `parallel` with `stepover 0.6`, ball Ø6, `tol 0.05`, `clearance_z 30`. Vertical feed moves near the hole centers:

| | fill off | fill on (current) | fill on (fixed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| near the holes | 22 | 166 | 40 |
| elsewhere | 36 | 128 | 57 |

(The `fill off` path is byte-identical baseline; the fix cuts the lid-induced plunges by ~75%.)

## The fix

One plane per opening: before emitting, lift the whole lid — the raised component **and** its one-cell ring — to the highest closed height over all of those cells (`Grid::plateau` in `fill.rs`). The plateau runs *after* the `enclosed` check, so enclosure is still judged against the closing's own levels. Doc-law updated: "One plane per opening" now covers the ring cells.

Regression test: `a_pocket_under_a_descending_roof_gets_one_flat_lid` in `crates/motion/tests/finish3d_land.rs` — a pocket under a shallow descending roof must come out coplanar, and the land never descends into the pocket.

## Bounded residuals (documented, not solved here)

Two narrow `None` zones remain at the lid/model boundary on the repro part, both inherent to tops-only lids:

- west rim: x ∈ [25.17, 25.40], **0.23 mm** — free-edge seating artifact where the lid is flush with the roof (7.085 vs 7.0848);
- east rim: x ∈ [31.76, 33.23], **1.47 mm** — the roof descends eastward (~0.27 mm drop to the ring's last cell), and a flat lid over a sloping roof always steps down to the real surface at its edge.

Both are ball-seating artifacts at the step, not interior churn. A follow-up giving lids side faces (or edge support at lid boundaries) could close them; I'm leaving that out of this fix since each residual is bounded and at most one extra plunge per rim crossing.

Also out of scope here: the V-crease being treated as a third opening (the depth-guard idea from the #1286 review) — that stays separate.

title: Mazak post writes the spindle start and stop as MOTON S.. / MOTOFF - not ISO 6983 words, no direction before a G84; which Mazak document gives them?

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

The Mazak post starts and stops the spindle with `MOTON S..` and `MOTOFF` in every section:

```
T2 M6
G43 H2
MOTON S600
M8
G00 X0 Y0 Z20
G99
G84 X0 Y0 Z8 R20 F600
G80
G00 X0 Y0 Z45
M9
MOTOFF
```

These are the only multi-letter words in the program. The post's own header gives its grammar as "public RS-274/ISO 6983 documentation". In that grammar a word is an address letter followed by a number (`M3`, `S600`), so `MOTON` and `MOTOFF` are not words of it.

`MOTON` also states no direction. The block after it is a right-hand rigid tap (`G84`), which needs the spindle turning clockwise.

## Reproduction (main 38699549, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

`assets/posts/mazak.cps` is unchanged from there to 3f6ecb4a.

The part is a Ø36 × 20 disc with a Ø5 blind hole to z 4. On the built-in `VMC 3-axis`:

- **D1:** Drill with `cycle: "peck"`, `peck: 2`.
- **D2:** Drill with `cycle: "drill"`, `dwell: 0.5`.
- **T1:** Drill with `TAP-M6`, `cycle: "tap"`, threaded to z 8.

`generate` and `verify` are clean. `post` with `"post": "Mazak"` writes 49 lines, with `MOTON S7500` / `MOTON S600` and `MOTOFF` around each section as above. The words have been in the post since it shipped (4288300f, M3.3 B), and the goldens under `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/mazak/` lock them.

## Neighbour case

The same stream through the other Fanuc-family posts (`Fanuc`, `Haas`, `doosan-dnm.cps`, `tormach.cps`) writes `S600 M3` before the tap and `M5` at section end.

## Root cause (unknown)

The header credits the words to "the control family's published operator conventions" ("spindle-logic M words MOTON/MOTOFF with the speed on the same block"), but names no document. I found no public Mazak EIA/ISO material that uses them. If a Mazak control does not accept them, every program from this post fails at its first spindle start. That is either an alarm, or feeds with the spindle stopped if the block is skipped.

Which published Mazak document gives `MOTON` / `MOTOFF` as the spindle start and stop words?

## Suggested labels

Outside contributors can't set labels, so these are suggestions:

- `P1` if the words are not Mazak's (wrong posted G-code in every Mazak program). The question above settles that.
- `effort:high`: posted G-code.
- `area:post`
- `source:agent`

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Doosan DNM 5700 machine states Z travel -510..0 (machine frame): every move above the work origin is refused at the post, as in #457

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

On the built-in **Doosan DNM 5700** machine, the post gate refuses every move above the work origin's Z0: every clearance, retract and cut above the origin. The cause is that its Z travel is stated in the machine frame. A plain face job's first rapid already fails:

```
post: post blocked - machine Doosan DNM 5700: 40 limit problem(s): F1: move 0 reaches 35.000 in Z, the stroke is -510.000..0.000; F1: move 1 reaches 10.000 in Z, the stroke is -510.000..0.000; ...
```

This is the #457 defect, which `vmc.mch` and `tilthead.mch` were fixed for, in the machine registered later by #614.

## Reproduction (main 38699549, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

`assets/machines/doosan-dnm.mch` and `crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs` are unchanged from there to 3f6ecb4a.

```json
[["load_machine", {"builtin": "Doosan DNM 5700"}],
 ["set_stock", {"box": {"dx": 60, "dy": 40, "dz": 10}}],
 ["add_tool", {"catalog": "EM-1000-4FL"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "face", "tool": "EM-1000-4FL", "name": "F1"}],
 ["generate", {"name": "F1"}], ["verify", {}],
 ["post", {"output": "f1.nc", "post": "Doosan DNM"}]]
```

`verify` returns one `post_gate` finding (`blocks_post: true`) with the 40 limit problems, and `post` refuses with them as quoted above.

## Neighbour case that works

The same calls with `{"builtin": "VMC 3-axis"}` and the `Fanuc` post: `verify` is clean, and the post writes 40 lines (`G00 X-35 Y-15 Z35`, `G01 ... Z10 F300`, ...). The program is the same; only the machine's stated bands differ.

## Root cause (confirmed)

`assets/machines/AGENTS.md` (the `travel` bullet) says:

> a stroke in PROGRAM coordinates ... The file cannot know the work offset, so a linear slide of stroke L is written `-L..L` - the FULL stroke each way, never the machine-frame band (`-500..0` for a 500 mm column refuses every retract above the work origin, #457 ...)

`doosan-dnm.mch` states:

- **Z:** `{ "min": -510.0, "max": 0.0 }`, the machine-frame band. The limit check (`crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs`, the travel loop) reads `(w - origin) * sign` against it, so every move above the work origin fails.
- **X and Y:** `-510..510` and `-285..285`, half the catalog strokes in the file's own description ("X/Y/Z: 1020/570/510mm"). The rule's full-stroke-each-way form is `-1020..1020` and `-570..570`. As stated, a program whose work origin sits at a table corner is refused once it runs past 510 mm in X or 285 mm in Y.

Every other shipped mill file states a symmetric Z band (`vmc.mch` and `tilthead.mch` ±500, `grblhal-3axis.mch` ±100, the Tormach, Sienci and Carvera files ± their figures). `load_machine` derives the table from the same numbers: `"table": {"max": [510.0, 285.0, -510.0], ...}`.

## Expected

The DNM file follows the travel rule: `-1020..1020`, `-570..570` and `-510..510`. The face job posts as it does on the built-in VMC. A test like `crates/app/tests/vmc_stroke.rs` (#477) pins it.

## Suggested labels

Outside contributors can't set labels, so these are suggestions:

- `P3`: a legal program on a shipped machine is refused. Another machine is the only workaround.
- `effort:high`: the fix is a data change plus a pinning test, but it moves the travel and collision laws, so the safety floor applies.
- `area:post`
- `source:agent`

title: A new lathe Facing faces the part away: the seed's facing plane is Bottom of Model and its top is Top of Model, so the stock allowance is never faced

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:turning
labels.description: Lathe and mill-turn

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

A lathe Facing created with its seed heights faces the part away down to its bottom, and leaves the stock allowance above the part untouched. The seed sets:

- `top_z` to Top of Model.
- `bottom_z`, the finished facing plane, to Bottom of Model.

The MCP `add_operation` creates from `operation::seed_params` (#511). The GUI's quick-add (`quick_params`) retypes the same Face draft, so it gets the same heights. Only the MCP path was run.

`generate` says `ok`. `verify` holds the post, but its words understate the cut: "0.8000 mm gouge" for passes that cut 48 mm into the part.

## Reproduction (main 38699549, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

`crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs`, `crates/app/src/operation/seed.rs` and `crates/motion/src/turning/face.rs` are unchanged from there to 3f6ecb4a.

The part is a plain bar, r 10 from z 0 to 48: an ASCII STL revolved from the meridian `(0,0) (10,0) (10,48) (0,48)` with 64 segments. The stock is a cylinder of 20 × 50, so 2 mm of facing allowance stands above the part.

```json
[["load_machine", {"path": "assets/machines/lathe.mch"}],
 ["import_model", {"path": "cyl.stl"}],
 ["set_stock", {"cylinder": {"diameter": 20, "height": 50}}],
 ["add_tool", {"catalog": "TN-1600-0R8"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "facing", "tool": "TN-1600-0R8", "name": "F1", "source": "cyl"}],
 ["generate", {"name": "F1"}], ["verify", {}],
 ["post", {"output": "f1.nc", "post": "assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps"}]]
```

- `get_job` shows the seed: `"top_z": {"offset": 0.0, "reference": "top_of_model"}, "bottom_z": {"offset": 0.0, "reference": "bottom_of_model"}`.
- `generate` returns `status: ok` with 487 moves. That is 97 stations at the 0.5 stepdown, from z 0 up to z 48.
- `verify` returns:
  ```
  finish envelope near move 3: 0.8000 mm gouge, 0.0092 mm rest
  rapid move 4 travels below the clearance plane inside stock
  rapid move 5 travels below the clearance plane inside stock
  ```
- `post` is refused: `post blocked - 3 warning(s): ...`

## Neighbour case that works

On the same document, `edit_operation` with `top_z` = Top of Stock and `bottom_z` = Top of Model gives 27 moves and no findings. It posts 42 lines: five passes `X-1.6` at Z50, Z49.5, Z49, Z48.5 and Z48.

## Root cause (confirmed)

`seed_facing` (`crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs`) takes `top: c.top` and `bottom: c.bottom` from `Carried::of` the seed Face. Face has neither field, so the fold's defaults fill them: `Height::of(TopOfModel, 0.0)` and `Height::of(BottomOfModel, 0.0)`. The second is the #214 choice ("the part's own floor") made for the mill kinds' depth.

For Facing that floor becomes the facing plane. `turning::facing` then ladders from `facing_z` = 0 up to `min(top_z, z_top)` = 48, so the allowance above 48 is never reached and every station below it cuts the part.

`seed_facing` already overrides the fold's stepdown for this family ("the mill default the fold carries would refuse against the house insert's 0.8 mm nose"). The heights get no such override. The test `the_facing_seed_faces_the_bar` (`crates/app/tests/turning.rs`) passes `top` and `bottom` as fixed 16 and 14 in a hand-built `Carried`, so it never meets the fold's defaults.

On the verify wording: `EnvelopeReport::gouge_mm` saturates at the ball radius by design ("a path that buried its centers in material reads the saturation value `r`"). So the reported 0.8 mm is the nose radius, not the depth cut.

## Expected

A new Facing faces the allowance down to the part's top: Top of Stock down to Top of Model, the heights of the neighbour case. When the part is already at length, it says there is nothing to face.

## Suggested labels

Outside contributors can't set labels, so these are suggestions:

- `P3`: every new Facing cuts the part away until its heights are edited. The gate catches it, so it is not P1.
- `effort:high`: a small diff (one seed in `kinds.rs`, plus a test that runs `seed_params` itself), but it changes what a new op posts, so the safety floor applies.
- `area:turning`
- `source:agent`

title: Lathe Facing on a grooved bar is refused at the post: the sphere-envelope scan counts the groove floor across the spindle as rest

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:turning
labels.description: Lathe and mill-turn

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

A lathe Facing that only faces the end of a bar is refused at the post when the bar has a groove anywhere along it. The same Facing on a plain or stepped bar posts. `verify` reports the groove as unremoved rest belonging to the Facing:

```
F2: finish envelope near move 3: 0.0000 mm gouge, 17.0528 mm rest   (blocks_post: true)
post: post blocked - 1 warning(s): F2: finish envelope near move 3: 0.0000 mm gouge, 15.5616 mm rest
```

The groove lies 11 mm below the faced band. No Facing can reach it, and the Groove kinds exist to cut it.

## Reproduction (main 38699549, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

`crates/sim/src/verify/finish.rs`, `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/`, `crates/motion/src/turning/` and `crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs` are unchanged from there to 3f6ecb4a.

The bars are closed revolves about Z with 64 segments, written as ASCII STL from a meridian of (r, z) points:

- **plain:** `(0,0) (10,0) (10,48) (0,48)`
- **stepped:** `(0,0) (10,0) (10,20) (7,20) (7,40) (5,40) (5,48) (0,48)`
- **wider at the free end:** `(0,0) (7,0) (7,20) (10,20) (10,48) (0,48)`
- **groove:** `(0,0) (10,0) (10,34) (5.5,34) (5.5,37) (10,37) (10,48) (0,48)`
- **groove near the top:** `(0,0) (10,0) (10,44) (8,44) (8,46) (10,46) (10,48) (0,48)`
- **shaft:** `(0,0) (10,0) (10,20) (7,20) (7,34) (5.5,34) (5.5,37) (7,37) (7,40) (5,40) (5,48) (0,48)`

```json
[["load_machine", {"path": "assets/machines/lathe.mch"}],
 ["import_model", {"path": "<bar>.stl"}],
 ["set_stock", {"cylinder": {"diameter": 20, "height": 50}}],
 ["add_tool", {"catalog": "TN-1600-0R8"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "facing", "tool": "TN-1600-0R8", "name": "F2", "source": "<bar>",
   "params": {"top_z": {"offset": 0, "reference": "top_of_stock"}, "bottom_z": {"offset": 0, "reference": "top_of_model"}}}],
 ["generate", {"name": "F2"}], ["verify", {}],
 ["post", {"output": "f2.nc", "post": "assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps"}]]
```

The Facing generates 27 moves on each bar: five stations from z 50 down to z 48.

| Bar | `verify` | Post |
|---|---|---|
| plain | no findings | written (42 lines) |
| stepped | no findings | written (with Profile Rough + Finish: 829 lines) |
| wider at the free end | no findings | - |
| groove | `0.0000 mm gouge, 17.0528 mm rest` | blocked |
| groove near the top | `0.0000 mm gouge, 10.2818 mm rest` | blocked |
| shaft | `0.0000 mm gouge, 15.5616 mm rest` | blocked |

## Root cause (confirmed)

Facing's registry row is `mode: Mode::Envelope` (`crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs`, Facing `KindInfo`). Its comment reads: "a meridian circle revolved IS a sphere about the axis, so the scan reads the lathe's own cut". `finish_envelope` (`crates/sim/src/verify/finish.rs`) then runs `stock_sim::envelope_scan_centers` over the pass as it lies in world space, a radial line in the y = 0 half-plane x ≥ 0. The scan never turns the work.

The scan's `rest_mm` includes "material standing hidden under an occluding top" (M2.2d, `EnvelopeReport::rest_mm` in `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/scan.rs`). A groove's floor is an upward face under the bar's full diameter above it, so it counts. Every reported figure equals the distance from the groove floor's outer rim on the far side of the axis (x = −r_rim, y = 0, z = floor) to the last pass's nose centre at the axis (0, 0, 48 + 0.8), less the 0.8 nose:

| Bar | Floor rim | √(r_rim² + (48.8 − z_floor)²) − 0.8 | Reported |
|---|---|---|---|
| groove | r 10, z 34 | 17.06 | 17.0528 |
| groove near the top | r 10, z 44 | 10.29 | 10.2818 |
| shaft | r 7, z 34 | 15.57 | 15.5616 |

The figures sit slightly below the true-circle values because the 64-gon floor rim is a chord.

The Groove rows of the same table already say why a sphere scan cannot judge this ("No sphere can judge a band: a grooved part is undercut BY DESIGN"), and they use `Mode::Revolve`.

Seen on the same shaft, but not root-caused: Profile Rough and Profile Finish (also `Mode::Envelope`) report `12.7553 mm rest` and `0.0073 mm gouge, 12.4890 mm rest` with default heights. A stepped bar without a groove gives them no findings.

## Expected

A Facing is judged on the band it claims, as the turned work sees it. A groove elsewhere on the bar is not its rest, and the program posts as it does on a bar without the groove.

## Suggested labels

Outside contributors can't set labels, so these are suggestions:

- `P3`: a legal turning program is refused.
- `effort:high`: verifier logic; the safety floor.
- `area:turning`
- `source:agent`

title: 3D Finish and 3D Pocket refuse the sample STEP laid flat: two solids sharing a face slice as "non-manifold contact", reported as invalid machining parameters

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

`testdata/models/sample_ap214.step` laid flat (rotated -90° about X) cannot be machined by any 3D operation. 3D Finish and 3D Pocket are both refused before any toolpath is planned:

```
generate: S1 - could not generate the toolpath: S1: invalid machining parameters: chords meet 3+ ways at z = 1.8359437500001423: non-manifold contact
generate: R1 - could not generate the toolpath: R1: invalid machining parameters: chords meet 3+ ways at z = 1.8359437500001423: non-manifold contact
```

The model is a valid STEP file. The message blames "machining parameters", but no parameter is at fault, and nothing tells the user what is wrong with the model or what to change.

## Reproduction (main 38699549, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

`slice.rs`, `slice_weld.rs`, `crates/app/src/operation/` and `crates/motion/src/machining3d/` are unchanged from there to 3f6ecb4a.

```json
[["import_model", {"path": "testdata/models/sample_ap214.step"}],
 ["move_model", {"name": "sample_ap214", "position": [0, -26.7192, 1.5875], "rotation": [-0.7071067811865476, 0, 0, 0.7071067811865476]}],
 ["set_stock", {"box": {"dx": 70, "dy": 124, "dz": 8}}],
 ["add_tool", {"catalog": "BN-0600"}],
 ["add_tool", {"catalog": "EM-0600-4FL"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "finish3d", "tool": "BN-0600", "name": "S1", "source": "sample_ap214"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "pocket3d", "tool": "EM-0600-4FL", "name": "R1", "source": "sample_ap214"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "contour", "tool": "EM-0600-4FL", "name": "C1", "source": "sample_ap214"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "pocket", "tool": "EM-0600-4FL", "name": "P1", "source": "sample_ap214"}],
 ["generate", {"name": "S1"}], ["generate", {"name": "R1"}],
 ["generate", {"name": "C1"}], ["generate", {"name": "P1"}]]
```

S1 and R1 are refused as quoted above. The Parallel and Waterline patterns of 3D Finish give the same refusal.

## Neighbour cases that work

- The same model in the same placement, with 2D Contour C1 and 2D Pocket P1: both generate (`status: ok`, 52 and 748 moves).
- A throwaway test called `geometry::slice::slice` on `model::world_facets` of the laid-flat model, every 0.05 mm in Z. The model is three solids (`MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` 'Part 1' to 'Part 3'). It was split into bodies by shared vertices:

| Facets sliced | Z span (mm) | Planes refused |
|---|---|---|
| all three solids | 0 .. 6.5278 | 32 of 129 (z 1.60 .. 3.15) |
| body 0 alone (1758 facets) | 0 .. 3.1750 | 0 of 62 |
| body 1 alone (968 facets) | 1.5875 .. 4.7625 | 0 of 62 |
| body 2 alone (452 facets) | 0.1778 .. 6.5278 | 0 of 126 |
| bodies 0 + 1 | 0 .. 4.7625 | 32 of 94 (z 1.60 .. 3.15) |
| bodies 0 + 2 | 0 .. 6.5278 | 0 of 129 |
| bodies 1 + 2 | 0.1778 .. 6.5278 | 0 of 126 |
| all three, as imported (not rotated) | -32.357 .. 85.851 | 0 of 2363 |

The refused band is exactly where bodies 0 and 1 overlap in Z: 1.5875 .. 3.175.

## Root cause (confirmed)

`slice()` in `crates/geometry/src/geometry/slice.rs` (step 2, lines 158-180) requires every chord end to be shared by exactly two chords. Bodies 0 and 1 share a cylindrical face of radius 17.5146 mm about the model's XY origin (0, -26.7192), and both solids carry identical tessellation vertices on it. Laid flat, that face stands vertical. Every plane through the two bodies' common height therefore cuts both section outlines through the same points. At z = 2.0 there are 93 such points, all at r = 17.5146, each the end of four chords (two from each body). The exact weld returns `SliceError::NonManifold` there.

That refusal comes before step 4 (`Region::from_slices`), whose comment reads "the non-zero fuse unites shells". As imported, the cylinder's axis is horizontal, and every plane slices (last row of the table).

`from_slice` in `crates/app/src/operation/material.rs:250` and `crates/motion/src/machining3d/rest.rs:23` then maps the refusal to `GenError::Invalid`. That error prints as "invalid machining parameters: …".

### Related

M13.11 already reads a plane as the union of touching bodies, but only for a selection across several models:

- `Material.bodies` (`crates/app/src/operation/material.rs`) is filled only in `material_of`'s `SrcRef::Selection` arm.
- `verify::verify_bodies` and `machining2d::contour_on_bodies` read it.

A single model holding several solids arrives as `SrcRef::Entity`, so `bodies` stays empty. `material::section()` then slices its facets plainly.

## Expected

Solids of one model that touch along a face slice as their union; each solid slices on its own at every one of those planes. If a section really cannot be built, the refusal names the model and says its solids touch at that height, instead of blaming machining parameters.

## Suggested labels

Outside contributors can't set labels, so these are suggestions:

- `P3`: a legal 3D job on a shipped sample model is refused, with a misleading message.
- `effort:high`: slicer behaviour; the geometry safety floor.
- `area:3d`
- `source:agent`

title: Explain G-code: the one word table gives lathe posts mill meanings - G98/G99 read as cycle returns, T0101 as TOOL 101

labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
**What happens.** `explain()` (`crates/post/src/post/explain.rs`, from #1394) explains every post's words from one table, `_EXPLAIN_WORDS`, keyed by the word alone. Two shipped lathe posts write words that mean something else on their control:

- `fanuc-lathe.cps` writes `G99` as feed per revolution (`onOpen`, line 368: `// unit, ZX plane, no nose comp, feed/rev`) and `G98` as feed per minute (C-axis live tooling, line 553). The table says G98 = `CYCLE RETURNS TO START HEIGHT`, G99 = `CYCLE RETURNS TO R HEIGHT`.
- `fanuc-lathe.cps` (line 428) and `tormach-lathe.cps` (line 383) write `T0101`: tool/station 1, offset 1. `_explainWord` reads the whole number: `TOOL 101`.
- `fanuc-lathe.cps` writes `G50 S<rpm>` as the spindle speed clamp (lines 432, 445, 458). G50 is not in the table, so the block is explained as `SPEED 3000` alone, which reads as a speed command.

**Reproduction** (main `38699549`). A test post that declares `explains = "paren"` and whose `block()` appends `explain(words)` (the shape `crates/post/tests/explain.rs` uses) was fed the blocks fanuc-lathe writes and posted through `engine::run_with` with `{"Explain": true}`:

```
G21 G18 G40 G80 G99 (MM UNITS, XZ PLANE, RADIUS COMP CANCEL, CANCEL DRILL CYCLE)
T0101 (TOOL 101)
G50 S3000 (SPEED 3000)
G96 S200 M3 (CONSTANT SURFACE SPEED, SPEED 200, SPINDLE ON CLOCKWISE)
G98 (CYCLE RETURNS TO START HEIGHT)
G99 (CYCLE RETURNS TO R HEIGHT)
G95 (FEED PER REVOLUTION)
G76 P010060 Q50 R0.02 (THREADING CYCLE)
```

Neighbour cases that read right: `G95` (tormach-lathe's feed per revolution) and `G76` (both lathes' threading cycle). On the mill posts `fanuc.cps` and `doosan-dnm.cps`, G99 does mean the R-plane return (#994).

**Reach today.** No shipped post declares `explains` yet, so no posted program carries these comments. #1388 names `fanuc-lathe.cps` and #1387 names `tormach-lathe.cps` among the posts that opt in next, so they would be the first to write them.

**Root cause (confirmed):** the meanings are one table keyed by word, with no way for a post to say what a word means on its control. The #1386 decision file sources the wording from RS-274 / ISO 6983 and the LinuxCNC lists, where G98/G99 are the canned-cycle returns. `_explainWord` also reads a `T` word as a single number.

**Done means:** a lathe post that opts into Explain never writes a mill meaning for G98/G99, never reads T0101 as tool 101, and never presents `G50 S` as a plain speed. One way: a post states its own meanings for the words its control reads differently, or the words to leave unexplained. Pin it with a test that posts G98, G99, G50 S and T0101 through fanuc-lathe with Explain on.

Suggested labels (an outside contributor cannot set them): `P7` while no lathe post explains (it becomes a misleading comment, `P3`, once #1387 or #1388 wires one), `effort:medium`, `area:post`, `source:agent`.

body:
**Found in a PathPilot Hub run (770MX sim, v2.14.4, 2026-11-12).** The Tormach golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/drill_peck.nc` (and its inch twin) alarms at line 9:

```
G73: Cannot feed with zero feed rate
  in drill_peck_inch.nc: line 9: G73 X0.7874 Y0.3937 Z-0.9449 R0 Q0.7087
```

**Cause.** The golden is posted from the CL fixture `drill_peck.cl`. Its `; CYCLE Peck ...` record has no feed, and the fixture has no tool record. `CycleRec::props` passes `FeedRate: null`. `tormach.cps` `onCycle` then calls `fw(p.FeedRate)`, which writes nothing, and posts a G73 with no F. The same fixtures also post no `T.. M6`, `S..` or `M3`. So `contour_plate_with_hole.nc` cuts its G1/G2/G3 moves with the spindle never started. In Hub that showed as T0 and spindle 0 rpm, and it still ran to M30.

**Why it matters.** A real CamCraft program carries the tool's feed and spindle, so this has not been seen from the GUI. But the post fails open. Under the Prime Directive, a stream that asks for a feed cycle without a feed, or for a cut with no spindle on, should be refused by name and not posted. On a control that keeps a modal F from an earlier block, a missing F on a canned cycle drills at whatever feed was last in force.

**Done means:**
- `tormach.cps`, and every post with the same `fw()` pattern on cycles, refuses a canned cycle whose `FeedRate` is missing or not positive, by name.
- A feed move (G1/G2/G3, or a cycle) before any spindle start is refused by name. Spindleless dialects (plasma, laser) are exempt.
- The golden fixtures that post to Tormach state a tool, spindle and feed, so the Tormach goldens are real runnable programs. The goldens are regenerated, and the change is listed in the PR.
- Pinning tests: a cycle with no feed is refused; a cut with no spindle start is refused.

Hub evidence: the user's screenshots, 2026-11-12 19:43-19:47.

title: Sinker rough/finish: count the orbit radius in the undersize size law

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
Found while refreshing PR #1136 (#543, sinker rough and finish with undersize) over main's #544 (sinker orbit).

What happens now: #543's size law (`motion::sinker_undersize::judge`) sizes a rough or finish burn as electrode + 2 x spark gap per axis, and places the tip one undersize above the finished floor. #544's orbit moves the electrode a further `radius` sideways at the burn floor, so an orbited pass burns electrode + 2 x (gap + radius) wide. The law does not count that, so PR #1136 refuses an orbit on a rough or finish by name (`SinkerBurnOp::pass_refusal`, at command creation and at generate) instead of judging it wrongly. A plain single burn may still orbit.

What should happen: the common practice is that the electrode undersize per side covers gap + orbit, so a finish with an orbit should be judged as `e + 2(g + r) == c` (a rough: `<= c`), with the floor stand worked out so the floor is neither left short nor over-burned by the orbit, and the stock-sim verdict pinning both.

Done means: a Sinker Burn rough or finish accepts an orbit; `judge` counts the radius in the burned width; a finish with an orbit burns the cavity to size (sim verdict clean, 0 gouge, rest within the sim's resolution); an orbit that would push the walls past the cavity is refused by name; the refusal added in PR #1136 is removed; pins in `sinker_undersize` cover both.

Related: #543, #544, #547 (electrode from faces subtracts `orbit` in its size: PR #1156).

title: box_pick: two MCP tests share one pid-named temp dir and race (mcp_pick_in_box_adds_the_rim_in_one_undo_step flakes red)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

body:
What failed: the batch gate on main 872901a2 ended red on one test, `mcp_pick_in_box_adds_the_rim_in_one_undo_step` (crates/app/tests/box_pick.rs). Panic at line 220: `import_model refused: "import_model: I/O error: The system cannot find the path specified. (os error 3)"`. The other 6 tests of the binary passed.
Where: gate log `gate-logs/batch-20261113-021709/07-app_suites_slow_release_tier_center_cut_multiaxis_.log` (local, main checkout).

Cause (read from origin/main, not re-run): `write_plate_stl()` builds `temp_dir()/camcraft-box-pick-<process id>/plate.stl`, and it starts with `remove_dir_all(dir)` then `create_dir_all`. Two tests in the same binary call it (`mcp_pick_in_box_adds_the_rim_in_one_undo_step`, line 216, and `mcp_pick_in_box_is_visible_only_unless_through`, line 266). The dir name depends only on the pid, so both tests use the same directory. Under parallel test threads, one test's `remove_dir_all` deletes the dir (and the STL) the other has just written, and its `import_model` gets os error 3 (path not found).

Introduced by: the second test arrived with commit 8e820f01 "fix(pick): the box honours Pick through; MCP pick_in_box takes through" (PR #1078, issue #979); the helper itself is from 6716fad1 (same PR).

Deterministic? No, a race. It fails only when the two tests overlap in the window between write and import, so it is intermittent (hit once in this gate run, 6 of 7 passed).

Fix direction: give each call a unique dir (an atomic counter or the test name in the dir name, as other suites do), and do not rely on remove-then-create of a shared path.

Done means: `write_plate_stl` returns a path unique per call; `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test box_pick` passes repeatedly (e.g. 10 runs) with default threads.

What happens: `AlignPartToSetup::align_from_axes` with both +Y and +X picked builds the new alignment through the held one. Done means: re-applying the same two-axis picks refuses by name (pinned in `crates/app/tests/align_axes.rs` and/or `mcp_align_axes.rs`), and no tolerance change lets a real alignment change through as "already held".

title: Process: the merge-ready skill in the repo, on the deterministic merge planner

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Asked for by the maintainer, 2026-11-12: "we need the other agents to be able to run same skills and deterministic merge order functionality."

Today the skill that merges ready PRs lives only on the maintainer's machine (`~/.claude/skills/merge-ready/`), with its own Python planner. The repo has the rules (PROCESS_VERSION 31, PR #1227) and the planner (`cargo xtask merge-plan`), but no skill that uses them, so a fork's agents or another session cannot run the same procedure and may order merges differently.

## Wanted
1. **`.claude/skills/merge-ready/SKILL.md` in the repo**, ported from the local skill: preconditions (no cut in progress; repo rules win), collect (`merge-ready` PRs; only the owner's review marker and label count; draft / contradictory labels / moved heads handled through `merge-plan --delta` with its SAME / MECHANICAL / DELTA / NEW CODE classes), plan with `cargo xtask merge-plan`, ask the user yes/no per PR in groups (never merge what was not approved; never approve a PR), merge wave 1 in order with merge commits, then wave 2 one PR at a time (refresh, classify, merge before the next refresh), after-merge sweeps (issue labels, PROCESS_VERSION announcement), the report table, one gate per batch. It calls `cargo xtask merge-plan`, not a Python script. Who may run it: the maintainer's session merges; a fork's agents may run steps 1-2 read-only to see the plan for their own PRs.
2. **The planner is deterministic and says so.** The same set of PR heads and the same base must always give the same waves in the same order, on every OS: every choice has a total tie-break ending in the PR number, no hash-map iteration order leaks into the output, and the output states the base sha and each PR's head sha it planned against so two runs can be compared. Pin it: a unit test that shuffles the input order and gets the identical plan, and tests for each tie-break. `--json` output for other tools (waves, order, per-PR kind, conflicted files, shas).
3. **Parity with the reference** the maintainer has been using (`~/.claude/skills/merge-ready/scripts/plan_merge_order.py` on his machine - read-only reference, not part of the repo): stack and shared-history ordering, GitHub-only conflicts as "plain refresh", mechanical vs by-hand kinds, the UNKNOWN-mergeable wait and warning, octopus merges as NEW CODE. Say in the PR which differences remain and why.
4. AGENTS.md: one line where the merge rules are stated, naming the skill as the way a merge batch is run. `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` bumped; announcement text for #681 in the PR body.

Done means: an agent in a fresh clone can follow `.claude/skills/merge-ready/SKILL.md` end to end with only `gh`, `git` and `cargo xtask merge-plan`; two runs of the planner on the same heads print the same plan (pinned by tests); the skill never merges an unapproved PR and never refreshes a PR that is not next in the batch.

title: Verify: the overhang backstop of the mid-turn sweep (law c3) still samples 4 x 5 poses
