title: The browser (wasm32) build of CamCraft loads from the GitHub Pages site

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Asked for by the maintainer, 2026-11-12: "the wasm32 app should be loadable from the github pages for easy access". Filed by an agent for him (no `source:agent`: it is his request).

**Where things stand**
- GitHub Pages is now enabled for this repo (source: GitHub Actions) at https://neotech.github.io/Camcraft/. The `site` and `pages` jobs of `release.yml` build the Zola site in `site/` and deploy it on a release tag (#688). The `github-pages` environment allows `v*.*.0` tags to deploy.
- The wasm32 shell runs in a browser on WebGL2 (#31, PR #847): `web/build-app-wasm.sh --release` writes `<target>/web/` with `index.html`, `wasi_shim.js`, `camcraft-ui.js` and `camcraft-ui_bg.wasm`. Nothing publishes that folder; today it only runs from a local http server.
- The site's front page already says the browser build comes "once the app and its interface build for the web".

**What is wanted**
The released wasm32 build is served from the Pages site, so anyone can open CamCraft in a browser from a link, without installing anything.
- The app lives under a fixed path of the site (e.g. `/Camcraft/app/`), with a clear link from the front page and the guide's first-run page.
- It is built in the release workflow from the tagged tree (a job that runs `web/build-app-wasm.sh --release` and hands its output to the `site` job, which places it in the Pages artifact) - **no new `push`, `pull_request` or `schedule` trigger** (Actions budget). Linux runner; say in the PR how many billed minutes it adds to a cut.
- Everything the page loads resolves under the project sub-path (`/Camcraft/app/...`, not `/`): the import map, `wasi_shim.js`, the `.js`/`.wasm` pair, any asset fetch. A fork's own Pages (another owner or repo name) must work too, as the `site` job's `--base-url` already does.
- The page says what it is: the version it was built from, that it runs in the browser on WebGL2, and what does not work there yet (the list on #31: file picker, playback without threads, WebGPU).
- A failed wasm build must not withhold the docs site or the release: the docs deploy without `/app/` and the run names what failed (the way `publish` treats a failed platform build).

**Known obstacles**
- #949: the build script rewrites the checkout's `Cargo.lock`; in CI that must not leak into anything packaged from the same checkout.
- `.wasm` size and Pages limits (1 GB site, 100 MB per file): state the size in the PR; use `wasm-opt` if it is needed and available without a new unpinned download.
- Pages serves no custom headers (no COOP/COEP), so nothing may depend on `SharedArrayBuffer` / threads.

Done means: after a release tag, `https://neotech.github.io/Camcraft/app/` loads the shell of that release in a current Chrome and Firefox, linked from the site's front page; pinned by a check in the workflow that the Pages artifact holds `app/index.html` and the `.wasm`, and by a test or script check that the page's URLs are relative to its own folder.

Part of #688 (docs and browser build on Pages); builds on #31 (the app and UI on wasm).

title: Lathe holder body: the reach law reads the body at |X + x|, which is only right for a tool on the positive-X side

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:turning
labels.description: Lathe and mill-turn

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Noted by the high-tier review of PR #1043 (review comment on that PR, head 1a6d4017). The law is on main (#369); PR #1043 is what first lets a user reach it.

**What.** `Reach::radii` reads a lathe holder body point at radius `|X + x|`, where `X` is the tool tip's signed radial position and `x` the body point's radial offset in the turning tool frame. The UI and MCP wording says "+x points away from the spindle axis". Both are true only for a tip at X >= 0.

- Facing a little past centre (tip at a small negative X): `X + x` is still the body's real position, so the reading is right; only the wording is loose.
- A tool that really sits on the other side of the axis (a rear turret or gang position programmed at negative X), if any turning path can carry one: the body would be read mirrored through the axis, so a holder that hits could be judged clear.

**Not known.** Whether any turning operation or machine definition today can put a tip at a negative X other than the facing overrun. If none can, this is a wording fix plus a guard; if one can, it is a collision-law defect and should be re-rated P0.

Done means: it is stated (with a test) which signed-X cases the turning generators can produce; the law either handles a tip on the negative side correctly or refuses it by name; the UI/MCP wording says what +x means for both cases.

body:
Found while reproducing #1091 (and the reason the #1077 reviewer's probe got a second, unrelated refusal).

**What happens.** Import a casting, set the stock to "from model" with that casting as its source, import the part, and machine it. The casting stays in the tree as a model, and `stock_sim::part_facets_as_modelled` reads every non-fixture model as the part. So the program verdict judges the casting as finished geometry, and any cut into it - every cut, since the casting is the stock - is a gouge: `post blocked - gouge: program cuts below the model in 812 cell(s), worst 20.00 mm at (-1.75, -7.75, z 10.00)` (a Bore of a 16 mm hole in a part under a stepped casting, fixture of `crates/app/tests/stepped_stock_rapid.rs` without its `DeleteEntity` of the casting).

**Expected.** A model that is only the source of a `FromModel` stock is stock, not part: the verdict (and the field view) should not read it as finished geometry. (Possibly: a model that is the source of the stock and is not the source of any operation.)

**Workaround in the #1091 tests.** Delete the casting after `SetStock` - the stock keeps its own copy of the facets.

Done means: a casting used as from-model stock and left in the tree posts a legal program over a separate part, pinned by a test; a model that is both the stock source and an op's source (`edge_break_gate.rs`'s brick) keeps today's verdict.

body:
**What:** `solid_law_goldens::every_posted_golden_is_a_program_the_gate_passes` (#862, #1000) judges every posted `.nc` golden whose stem has a `.cl` golden. No operation kind, part, region or tool record makes it, so no gate a user's post runs can judge it. The guard can't tell a synthetic posting fixture from an op program nobody judged, so it keeps a by-name exception list.

**Why it matters:** a by-name exception list is where an unjudged op golden can hide later. A synthetic fixture should say what it is in the golden itself, the way a refused program carries the "refused program, posted for syntax conformance" first line.

**Done means:** posted goldens of hand-built posting fixtures (today `arc_planes` in Fanuc, haas, mazak, sinumerik, heidenhain) carry a first-line marker the guard recognises (e.g. "synthetic program, posted for syntax conformance"), written by the suite's regeneration path (`WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-app --test arc_planes`) and not by hand. Alternatively the fixture gets a part and a gate that judges it. `UNJUDGED` is then empty and removed, so any new unjudged posted golden fails the guard.

Found by the #1000 worker. Part of #1000's follow-up.

title: STEP import crashes (stack overflow) on a record with about 1000 nested parentheses

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Retired 2026-11-12: was the top priority; see P1

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
What happens: a STEP file whose DATA section holds one record with roughly 1000 or more nested `(` makes the import overflow the stack inside `ruststep`'s recursive-descent parser. The process dies - no error dialog, no diagnostic. It happens on main (a6bd69d8) with a valid header; found by the high-tier review of PR #1006 with a throwaway probe file (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/1006#pullrequestreview-5869273530). PR #1006 neither causes nor fixes it.

Why P0 (Prime Directive: "Degenerate input (... corrupt STL/STEP models) -> clean error, not a crash or hang"): opening a hostile or corrupt file takes the whole application down, unsaved work included. A stack overflow cannot be caught with `catch_unwind`.

Expected: such a file is refused by name ("STEP record nests deeper than N levels at entity #id, line L"), like every other corrupt file.

Ways to fix, to weigh in the decision file: (a) a cheap pre-scan of the DATA section that tracks parenthesis depth (outside strings and comments) and refuses past a stated cap before the parser runs - PR #1006's `step_diag.rs` already walks records and could host it; (b) parse on a thread with a large, bounded stack and treat its death as the refusal; (c) both. The STEP importer through solidcore (#916 / PR #941) caps parser nesting at 64 already - check the same input there and say so.

Also check the same class in the other importers the fuzz tests cover (STL, DXF if present): any recursive parser fed by file depth.

Done means: a fixture with a record nested 5000 deep is refused by name within a bounded time, in the default lane; a legitimately deep record under the cap still imports; the cap and its reason are recorded.

title: A thread mill on a model-sourced hole is convicted of a gouge on every helix move

labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found while working #1057 (on a full-fidelity model, so not a fidelity bug).

**What happens.** A Thread (thread mill) operation sourced from a model is convicted with `Gouge` on every helix move, and `Crossing` pairs, even at full fidelity. Fixture: `crates/app/tests/coarse_rims.rs` on `issue/1057-drill-excess-false-gouge` (PR for #1057) - the 40 x 40 x 20 block with a 20 x 20 cavity blind at Z 10, a 6 mm Tap-form thread mill (pitch 1), one `Hole { xy: (0,0), radius: 5.0, floor_z: 10.2 }`, `SrcRef::Entity("part")`: blocking warnings `Gouge { at: 4..=55 }` plus `Crossing { moves: [3, 56] } ...`.

**Likely cause.** The Thread kind verifies `Mode::Boundary` against the drill's rim region (`material_source::source_region`, Bore/Thread arm), and law (b) reads the declared rim at `r - tol`. A thread mill's helix runs the thread depth H (0.5413 x pitch) PAST the declared circle by design (`mill2d_c::thread_helices_are_timed_by_the_tools_pitch`: rho up to R + H - r), so every helix point reads as a gouge of about H against the rim. `mill2d_c` sources its threads from the stock, so it never sees this.

**What is owed.** Decide what a thread mill's rim is (the declared minor circle grown by the thread depth, or the major diameter) so a matched thread mill verifies clean against a model, while one cutting past the thread's major diameter still convicts; and look at the `Crossing` pairs on the same path.

**Done means:** a matched thread mill on a model-sourced hole verifies clean at full fidelity and near the refusal bound (`coarse_rims::a_thread_mill_reads_the_same_near_the_bound_as_at_full_fidelity` then tightens to `== Vec::new()`), and an oversize thread still convicts.

title: UI: native Open/Save dialogs can open behind the app window

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

body:
## What

Every native picker (Open, Model, Save, Save As, Post, machine/post/theme picks) could
open **behind** the CamCraft window: the rfd dialog was created without an owner, and the
shell never asked for the foreground. A dialog opened right after launch — when the app was
started from a terminal or a script — was the worst case: the shell itself was not the
foreground window, so neither it nor its dialog was visible.

Reproduced on Windows 11 at 125 % scaling with the v0.18.0 release build: launch the app,
press Ctrl+O, and the `#32770` "Open" dialog exists but sits under the shell.

## Why

`crates/ui/src/file_dialog.rs` built `rfd::FileDialog` with title/filters/directory only —
`set_parent` was never called, so Windows had no owner to keep the dialog above. The shell
also never called `focus_window`, so a launch from a terminal left the app behind it, and an
owned dialog follows its owner's place in the z-order.

## Done means

- The shell asks for the foreground once, after the window is created.
- Every native picker is owned by the shell window, and the owner is raised just before the
  dialog opens.
- The GPU refusal `MessageDialog` is owned too.
- Hand-checked: launch from a terminal, first Ctrl+O, the dialog is visible in front; repeat
  for Save and Model.

Native dialog ownership has no headless test: rfd modals are hand-test-only in this repo
(`egui_app/tests.rs` says so), so the evidence is the hand check plus the z-order probe.

title: A matched drill is falsely convicted of a gouge on a reduced-fidelity model flagged above ~0.0105 mm

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found while working #904 (pinning the containment solid law on a reduced-fidelity model). This is in the code PR #911 merged; #904's slice does not change it.

**What happens.** A drill matched to its hole, on a model flagged between about 0.0105 mm and 0.015 mm (the refusal bound), is convicted with `Gouge` at its first plunge, even when it stops well above the hole's floor. The gate then blocks the post with a gouge that is not there. Below about 0.0105 mm (a metre-unit file's 0.01 mm included) and at full fidelity it is clean.

**Repro.** A 40 x 40 x 20 block with a 20 x 20 blind hole to Z 10, a 4 mm drill (`DR-0400`), one `Hole { radius: 2.0, entry_z: 20.0, floor_z: 10.0 }`, Bottom Z 10.2:

| model imported at | blocking warnings |
|---|---|
| full fidelity, 0.008 ... 0.0105 mm | none |
| 0.011 mm, 0.012 mm, 0.0149 mm | `Gouge { at: 1 }` |
| 0.03 mm (refused by name at the gate) | none |

(`crates/app/tests/coarse_contain.rs` on #904's branch has the fixture; pass `Some(0.011)` and a bottom of 10.2.)

**Likely cause.** The section law (b) reads `floor = r - leave - cx.tightened(cx.gouge_tol)` (`sim` `verify/section.rs`). `GOUGE_TOL` exists to absorb the chord error of our own regions (`operation/material.rs`: "half the geo2d round-join chord error plus room for float chains"). A drill's region is the hole's rim as a polygon, so a matched drill's centre stands a few microns inside `r` by construction. Once the model's excess has taken more than about half the tolerance, what is left no longer covers that polygon's own sagitta, and the law convicts the drill against its own rim. The same may hold for other kinds whose regions carry our own chords (bore, thread mill, circular).

**What is owed.** Decide how law (b) should split its tolerance between our own discretization and the model's excess (for example: tighten only the part of the tolerance not spent on the region's own chord error, or build these rims finer), so an honest drill is not convicted on a model that is still judged.

**Done means:** a matched drill, bore and thread mill on a model flagged anywhere below the refusal bound verify clean, with a pin at 0.0149 mm; a real gouge there is still convicted.

| r7 bar (`adaptive_plans_the_developed_levels_under_the_load_and_kink_laws`) | 5.0 | refused past the budget (85-86 revolutions), rings | refused, rings | **the budget passes it: HSM-planned, 5 in-cut breaks of 5.0-6.2 deg - the pin is red** (on main and with #982's fix alike) |
| r7 bar | 5.5 | HSM, lifted | HSM, lifted | main: rings (refused for travel - the lift edge #982 fixes); with #982: HSM, lifted |
| window (`the_developed_window_reaches_the_planner_and_names_each_refusal`) | 6.0, 5.0 | refused past the budget after 86 revolutions | refused after 85 | **the budget passes them**: main refuses them for travel (the lift edge); with #982 they are HSM-planned at 18.8 % D, 0 breaks |

So `adaptive_plans_the_developed_levels_under_the_load_and_kink_laws` is green on main only because the budget refuses level 5.0 at this exact geometry; a 250 nm change of the rings lets it through, it is planned, and the pin fails on the kink law (the breaks themselves are #1050).

**Why it matters.** Same as #982: a plan choice that flips on a nanometre-scale input blocks #882 and any other change to the planner's geometry, and a pin that is green by coincidence proves nothing.

**What #982 does and does not do.** It removes the lift-acceptance edge (the r6.2 neck levels 5.7 / 5.2 are HSM-planned at every perturbation tried). It does not touch `budget.rs` or `grow.rs` (PR #953 owns the latter).

Done means: the budget's verdict on the rotary window's and the r7 bar's levels is the same under a 16 nm - 0.25 um perturbation of the openings, pinned by perturbed twins the way #982 pins the slot; whichever way level 5.0 of the r7 bar is decided, its pin states it.

**What happens.** When a developed neck band of `rotary_adaptive`'s bars is HSM-planned (kept in cut by microlift returns), two readings on the suite's 0.1 mm dexel stand past the laws the whole r7 bar is pinned to:

1. **Bore exit load.** The r6.2 bar's levels 5.7 and 5.2 both read **20.3 % D** (55.5 deg) at one move, the first turn out of the entry's bore (developed (21.7, 7.7) -> (20.8, 6.8) on 5.7). **Why it was not seen.** Until #982 these bands were refused for travel on most runs (the microlift acceptance flipped on a sliver), so the plans were rarely posted and never pinned. #982's PR pins the r6.2 levels at what they read (`R62_LOAD_FACTOR` 1.40, `R62_BREAKS` 3 in `crates/motion/tests/rotary_adaptive.rs`) and names this issue.

body:
PR #1032 (`Fixes #980`) found why two levels of the user's STEP bore fell back from the HSM plan to Offset rings: the entry orbit closed about 1e-15 mm off its own start, and the self-crossing check (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/guard.rs`) - which only skips NEIGHBOURING chords of one walk and tests exact signs - read the spiral leaving that point as crossing the orbit's first chord. The fix closes the orbit exactly (`rings.rs`, `circle`); the check itself is unchanged, on purpose.

Left open (high-tier review of #1032, https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/1032#pullrequestreview-5868873098): the check stays exact-sign, so any other pair of walks that share a point to within rounding (a spiral that returns to its seed, a microlift return landing on a chord end, a ring that starts on the previous one) can still be reported as "crosses itself" and send a good level to Offset rings by name. Safe, but a silent loss of the adaptive plan the user asked for.

Expected: a shared end point (two chords touching at a common vertex within a stated tolerance far below the cutting tolerance) is not a crossing; a real crossing still is (the figure-eight unit test must stay green). State the tolerance and why it cannot hide a real self-cut. Related: #982 (microlift acceptance is a knife edge), #1010 (plans differ across platforms) - all three are about exact float comparisons in the planner.

Done means: a `crates/motion` test with two walks that touch at a shared point 1e-12 mm apart is not reported as crossing; the figure-eight still is; the heavy pins do not move, or the move is explained.

body:
Part of #361. Found while making lathe holder bodies reachable from the tool editor and MCP.

**What happens.** A turning tool can carry a lathe holder body (#369), and every move is judged against the part and the standing stock (`operation/turning_holder.rs`: "What stands. The part, always, and the stock less every cut"). The setup's workholding and fixtures are not in that reading. For a turning operation the fixture laws (`workholding_warnings` in `operation/generate.rs`) still sweep the tool record's holder cylinder (`tool_body::judged` returns the record unchanged for a lathe-frame body), and a turning insert's holder cylinder is normally 0 x 0. So an offset holder that runs into the chuck jaws, a tailstock or a steady rest passes with no finding - while the operation no longer carries the "holder not judged" note, because a body is present.

**Why it matters.** A user who imported the vendor's holder model reads "judged" as "judged against everything". A holder striking the chuck is a crash.

**Fix.** Read the lathe body's clearance bands (`camcraft_tools::lathe_holder::LatheClearance`) against the setup's steel as well: workholding that turns with the part as its revolved envelope (same reading as the stock), standing steel (tailstock, steady rest) in the machine frame. Until a kind of steel can be read, say so by name on the operation (a note like the existing "holder not judged"), never silently.

**Done means:** an offset lathe holder that reaches a chuck-jaw fixture is a blocking finding naming the move; the same holder clear of it passes; steel the law cannot read is named in a note. Pinned at the app level.

body:
From the review of PR #990 (#891), non-blocking note: constant surface speed (G96) is clamped by the lower of the machine's `spindle_max` and the tool's `max_rpm`. There is no workholding limit: a chuck or collet has its own rated maximum rpm (often far below the spindle's), and the only place to state it today is the tool's `max_rpm`, which is the wrong owner (the same tool in a different chuck has a different limit).

**Why it matters:** under G96 the rpm rises as the diameter shrinks, so a facing pass toward the centre runs up to the clamp. A clamp above the chuck's rating is a safety hazard (jaws lose grip force at speed).

**Expected:** a setup on a lathe can state its workholding's maximum rpm. The G96 clamp (Fanuc `G50 S`, Tormach `G96 D`) and the G97 rpm check use min(machine, tool, workholding). An rpm above the workholding limit is refused by name, never silently capped. Undoable command plus MCP tool; old projects load with none.

**Done means:** a setup with a 2000 rpm chuck limit posts `G50 S2000` / `G96 D2000` for a G96 op whose tool and machine allow more, and refuses a G97 op asking 2500 rpm by name; pinned in `lathe_post_css`; round-trip pinned.

Depends on PR #990 merging (stack on it while it is open).

body:
Follow-up to #871 (refusal ghost for part-way refusals). The #871 PR adopted the ghost where the moves are in hand and the frame is already mapped to world by `run_job`. The remaining part-way refusals each need a frame map or a merge first, so they were listed in `docs/decisions/871-refusal-ghost-rest.md` rather than swept:

- **finishing3d raster / rings / swarf** (`raster.rs` `parallel`, `rings_and_tail`, `swarf_multi`): Rotary contour and parallel run these on frame-LOCAL facets (`multiaxis/rotary.rs` calls of `finishing3d::waterline` / `swarf`). First add `.map_err(GenError::without_ghost)` (or a `to_world` map) at those rotary calls, then adopt `with_ghost_moves(b.moves())`.
- **Rotary links and posing** (`rotary_links.rs` `radial_relink`, `rotary.rs` `posed`): rotary-local frame. Needs `f.to_world` plus the tip offset.
- **Face under an area turn** (`generate.rs` `turn_path(face_over(..)?, -turn)`): the refusal's spot (already today) and any ghost are in the turned frame. Map the spot and ghost back through `turn_path(-turn)`.
- **Cross drill app-side laws** (`cross_spindle.rs` `rapids_clear`, `cross_holder` on the spindle-shifted `t`): carry the ghost by the same shift `in_world` uses.
- **Nested refusals** (`machining3d/entry.rs` `pocket3d_air_split` material leg, `run_rest` rest ladder; `generate.rs` stitched contour runs): the inner refusal already carries its own ghost and `with_ghost` keeps it. Prepend the outer moves to it, which needs a small `Ghost` merge.
- **Multiaxis stamp / swarf link / curve walk, the rotary gate, the fixture route**: these are one-liners, but each needs its frame checked (posed or unposed world).

Done means: each site above either hands back its partial path in world coordinates (pinned by a test that its ghost lands where the part is) or is listed in a decision file with the reason. No generator's successful output changes, so goldens stay byte-identical.

Effort is `high` because it touches generator code (safety floor), even though the change is display-only.

Part of #261 (follow-up to #871).

body:
**What:** PR #999 (#862) adds the guard `solid_law_goldens::every_posted_golden_is_a_program_the_gate_passes`. Every posted NC golden whose stem has a `.cl` golden must verify clean, carry a "refused program, posted for syntax conformance" first line, or be named in `UNJUDGED` with a reason. Six goldens sit in `UNJUDGED`: the two slot goldens, `trochoid_slot_small`, `trace_plate_with_hole`, `arc_planes` and `plasma_plate_with_holes`. No test checks their posted programs against the gate the user's post would run. `plasma_plate_with_holes` isn't run through the plasma gate in this suite at all.

**Why it matters:** this is the risk #862 closed for two fixtures. A posted golden for a program the gate would refuse reads as "this output is right". Being in `UNJUDGED` means "not checked", not "checked clean".

body:
Found while writing the #926 per-post script suites.

**What is wrong.** `post --machine <file.mch>` (the command-line post, `crates/post/src/bin/post.rs`) hands the script `post::machine::script_props` of the raw file. `script_props` reads the static grammar (`kinematics.static.rotaries`, `kinematics.static.head.spindle.max`, `...toolStation.coolants`, `rapidRate`, ...). Every shipped machine in `assets/machines/` is a vendor kinematics tree (`kinematics.default.parts`), which the app first parses (`machine::parse_mch`) and then mirrors (`post::machine::mirror`) into that grammar. The binary parses the file only for its inverted-axis refusal and then drops the parsed machine, so the script sees no rotaries, no spindle limit, no coolant list, no rates.

Seen: `post --machine assets/machines/tilthead.mch fanuc.cps <tilted stream>` refuses "tilted move on a machine without a tilting rotary" although the file states A and B; posting the same stream with `mirror(parse_mch(..))` works (the #926 suites do that as a workaround, see `crates/post/tests/recorded/mod.rs`).

Why P1: the CLI posts a different program for the same machine than the app does (missing spindle cap, coolant codes and rotaries; refusals where the app posts).

Done means: the binary posts with the mirrored machine (keeping the raw file for `invert::apply`), so `post --machine <vendor .mch>` gives the app's program; pinned by a CLI test on `tilthead.mch`; the #926 runner then passes the file straight through.

body:
Found by the #926 per-post script suites (recorded stream `drill_retract`: two pecked holes, R plane Z1, hop between holes Z3, clearance Z10).

**What is wrong.** The canned-cycle posts - `fanuc`, `haas`, `mazak`, `sinumerik`, `tormach`, `doosan-dnm` - move from one hole to the next at the R plane, not at the hop / clearance height the toolpath (and so verify and the stock simulation) uses:

```
G00 X10 Y10 Z1          <- the stream's rapid down to R is posted before the cycle
G98                     <- "return to the initial level" - which is now Z1, the R plane
G73 X10 Y10 Z-20 R1 Q4 F60
G80
G73 X30 Y10 Z-15 R1 Q4 F60   <- X10 -> X30 traverse at Z1; the path hops at Z3
```

The cycle swallows the chain's hop rapids (`Rapid Z3`, `Rapid X30 Z3`, `Rapid Z1`), and G98 returns to the level the tool stood at when the first cycle block was read. `fanuc.cps` says "The chain retracts to its initial (clearance) level each hole", but the dump posts move 0 (the rapid from clearance down to R) as an ordinary G00 before the cycle record (AT 1), so the initial level is R. Sinumerik writes no G98/G99 at all and lands the same way. The committed app golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/drill_plate.nc` already shows it: R0 there, so the posted program rapids from X10 to X30 at Z0 - the stock top - while `drill_plate.cl` hops at Z5.

Why P0: the posted traverse is lower than the motion that was simulated and judged. A hop height exists to clear something between holes (a clamp, a boss, stock above the model top); the program drives through it at rapid.

Heidenhain and Carvera post the expanded chain and are correct.

Done means: every canned-cycle post traverses between holes at the stream's hop level and leaves the last hole at its retract (e.g. initial level = the hop/clearance plane with G98, or G99 with the R plane and an explicit hop), pinned by the #926 `drill_retract` goldens of all six posts (now listed as known bugs in `crates/post/tests/recorded/mod.rs`) and the app golden `nc/drill_plate.nc`.

title: Thread milling: refuse a hole the program has not drilled yet (the mill is not centre-cutting)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Part of #894.

A thread mill is not centre-cutting, and the thread-milling ride (`machining2d::thread_ride`) feeds it down the hole's axis before the first lead-in arc. That is air only if an earlier operation opened the hole. Nothing checks it: the `Thread` operation generates and verifies clean on a part whose hole is modelled, even when the program holds no drilling operation before it and the stock at the hole is solid. The gouge laws read the part (the hole is in the model), so they see nothing; the centre-cutting audit (`operation::plunge_solid`, `camcraft_motion::plunge_law`) is not asked for this kind, and it reads the raw stock, which would refuse every thread.

**Effect:** forget the tap drill and the program plunges a thread mill into solid metal at plunge feed - a broken cutter, with no finding at generate, at verify or at the post gate.

**Fix sketch:** read the stock the setup's earlier operations leave standing (the prior grid the drilling laws already read, `operation::drill_prior`) under each threaded hole: the tool's full cylinder down the axis and the first pass's lead-in must fall through air. Refuse by name at generate ("the hole at (x, y) is not drilled yet - add a drilling operation before the thread") and digest the program ahead in the stamp, so reordering the operations marks the thread Stale.

**Done means:** a Thread operation with no drilled hole under it is refused by name; the same operation after a Drill of at least the tool's diameter generates; moving the Drill after the Thread turns it Stale and refuses; pinned by an app test. The milled `Bore` ride's axis entry gets the same reading or its own issue.

Part of #894.

The thread-milling kernel (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/thread_mill.rs`, `thread_ride.rs`) cuts an external thread on a boss - depth 0.6134 x pitch (ISO 965-1), clockwise climb under M3, quarter-arc leads from one tool radius outside the centre circle - and is pinned by `machining2d::thread_tests` and the golden `thread_mill_external_single_form.cl`. **What is missing**
- A feature list for bosses: recognition of vertical convex cylinders (the hole recogniser reads concave ones only) or a pick, giving centre, major radius, top and shoulder Z.
- An `external` flag on the operation (params, file, page, MCP params), and the door's external half (a boss thinner than the thread is deep).
- The crest law for a boss: the static footprint region cannot judge a tool standing beside a boss that rises from a wider base, so the tangency law needs the model's section at depth with the thread depth as its allowance; the root law (`thread_op::root_cutter`) must take the external depth.
- The air around the boss: the ride feeds down beside it, which the stock and plunge laws must accept only where earlier operations cleared it.

**Done means:** a Thread operation set to external threads a modelled boss, verifies clean against the part and the stock left by the operations before it, and posts helical G2/G3 with Z; a boss thinner than the thread depth and a boss with no cleared air around it are refused by name; pinned by an app test and a golden.

title: Adaptive microlift acceptance is a knife edge: lift_returns compares equal half-degree readings, so a 16 nm geometry change flips the slot's plan

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found while working #882 (held branch `issue/882-adaptive-open-simplify` @ 70ac996f; see https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/882#issuecomment-6811353217).

**What happens:** `adaptive/lift.rs` `lift_returns` keeps the microlifted plan only when its worst reading is not above the spiral's, and both are read in half-degree steps. On main, the 60 x 14 slot reads 48.0 against 48.0. Any geometry perturbation, even a 16 nm thinning of the opening, makes the spiral read 47.5, so the lifted plan is dropped and the slot falls from HSM (15.7 % load) to Offset rings.

**Why it matters:** a plan choice that flips on a nanometre-scale input is a knife edge. It blocks #882's speedup (the bore goes from 115.6 s to 2.2 s) and any other change that perturbs the planner's geometry.

Done means: the acceptance compares within a stated tolerance, not on equal half-degree steps. A pinning test shows the slot keeps the same plan under a perturbation of the opening's area in the 16 nm to 0.25 um range, and no adaptive fixture's verdict changes on main.

Part of #882.

body:
The release gate tier for v0.18.0 (branch `release/v0.18.0`, tree = main f490458a plus release docs and snapshot goldens; logs `gate-logs/release-20261112-001136/`) is green in 13 of 14 steps and red in one test of the app heavy lane (release, `--ignored`):

```
test the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean ... FAILED
panicked at crates\app\tests\pocket3d_hsm.rs:100:5:
["adaptive: the HSM plan for this area crosses itself at (-1.66, -2.80) - Offset rings cut the level at Z 20.000 instead",
 "adaptive: the HSM plan for this area crosses itself at (-1.99, -0.13) - Offset rings cut the level at Z 10.000 instead"]
```

The test pins (since #850 / PR #865) that on `testdata/models/Milling-test.step` only the TOP level (Z 20) falls back from the HSM plan to Offset rings, and the exact path size (5530 moves, 5497 planar feeds, 600 arcs). Now the Z 10 level falls back too. The toolpath still verifies clean (no warnings) and the fallback is named in the notes, so this is not wrong output: it is a quality regression on the user's own part - one more level cut with Offset rings instead of the adaptive plan.

Most likely cause (to confirm by running the test at 575f02d8 and at its first parent): PR #839 (merged as 575f02d8) caps the STEP chord and so changes the imported mesh of this model; the level outline the planner works on is different. The heavy lane runs only at a cut, so nothing showed it when #839 merged. PR #865's review foresaw the tripwire ("the bore test now asserts exact move counts on purpose").

Two parts:
1. For the cut: re-measure the pin and say why (the test's own comment asks for that), keeping every safety assertion - no warnings, each rings level named in the notes and the status line, no "planning budget" / "too detailed" refusal. Test-only.
2. The real fix, after the cut: the Z 10 level of the bore gets its HSM plan back (why does the plan cross itself on the finer outline - near-duplicate vertices, a sliver, the arc fit of the outline?), or the reason it cannot is recorded.

Done means: the Z 10 level of `Milling-test.step` is planned by the HSM planner again and the pin says `fell.len() == 1` again, or a decision entry explains why two levels is right; the heavy lane is green.

body:
`list_features` (`crates/app/src/mcp/features.rs`, `faces_view`) prints a planar face's `normal` and `facing` from the feature's canonical plane normal (`feature::Face.normal`), not from the face's outward side. On a plain 40 x 40 x 15 box the bottom face reads `"normal": [0, 0, 1], "facing": "up"` - the same as the top. Side faces pair up the same way (both Y sides read `[0, 1, 0]`).

For a WCS pick that is a frame turned upside down - the tools themselves read the outward normal correctly (`pick::align::outward_normal`), but the agent was steered to the wrong face. Found while writing the #937 pin, which now tells faces apart by `bounds`.

Done means: a face row's `normal` (and `facing`) is the outward normal - the one `outward_normal` reads, placed where the part sits - or a refusal-shaped field when the winding is not decidable; a test pins top vs bottom and both sides of a box; the camcraft-mcp skill note about this caveat (added by #937) is removed.

body:
Found while working #885.

A tilted record at A0 then writes no A word, although the post never commanded A0 and the table may stand anywhere. Reproduced on main (f490458a) with `rotaryBrake: true`:

```
TOOL 1 T1 / SECTION / Rapid ... A 30000 / Feed ... A 30000 / ENDSECTION
TOOL 2 T2 / SECTION / Rapid ... A 0     / Feed ... A 0     / ENDSECTION
```

**Expected:** the first A of a program, and the first A after anything that may have moved the table, is written; the modal memory is the angle the post last wrote, never an assumed 0. (The G43.4 branch is not affected - its arm writes all three words.)

PR for #885 reads the held angle only from the A words a block actually wrote, so a non-TCP feed that turns from an A the post never placed is now refused by name when the A states a rate - but with no stated rate the wrong program above still posts.

Done means: a pinning test posting the two-tool stream above writes A0 for the second tool (and an opening A0), goldens moved only where an A word was missing, each listed.

title: M12.1: a machining mesh from solidcore-tess - largest mesh-to-surface deviation benched, and every planner shortfall a refusal

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
What is left of point 4 of #916 (tessellation), found while benching it.

Facts from the bench (`crates/kernel/tests/step_agreement.rs`, solidcore pin `55d0e7638b9e1ebbf91ab8c10657e595c114ecda`): solidcore now has a mesher, `solidcore-tess`, which meshes the STEP reader's B-rep record at a chord tolerance in millimetres. At the app's 0.005 mm cap it is watertight on every fixture when vertices are welded by exact position (truck's per-face meshes leave 854 open triangle sides on Milling-test.step and 3196 on sample_ap214.step by the same count), and its volume and area are closer to the exact solid than truck's (5.6e-5 against 1.2e-4 relative on Milling-test). It uses more triangles (6228 against 952).

Owed before #917 can make the app's mesh with it:

1. **The deviation that matters for a gouge check is not measured yet.** The bench compares volume, area, bounding box and watertightness. It does not measure the largest distance from the mesh to the exact surface. Bench it per fixture against the chord asked for (0.005 mm, and the caps of #689 / #864), for solidcore-tess and for truck's mesh, and pin the verdicts.
2. **Its own docs call it a display mesher** ("a display mesh decides nothing a model depends on: it is drawn, never measured"), and it reports what it could not do in `PlanStats` instead of failing: `unmeshed`, `lenient` (a face filled leniently so the display has no hole), `over_tolerance`, `edges_capped`, `unsampled_edges`. A machining import must turn every one of those into a named refusal or a reduced-fidelity flag (#864 / PR #911), never a silent mesh. Decide which, per entry, and pin each with a fixture that provokes it.
3. **Triangle budget.** The app caps facets (`MAX_FACETS`) and coarsens to stay inside memory. solidcore-tess has its own bounds; state how the app's budget maps onto them.
4. **wasm32.** `solidcore-tess` gates rayon off on wasm32 in its manifest; a wasm32 check of it has not been run from this workspace.

Everything stays inside `crates/kernel` until #917 (low coupling, #919).

Part of #27. Gates #917.

Done means: the deviation bench runs in the kernel's lane with its table pinned; each `PlanStats` shortfall has a decided outcome and a test; the answer on the triangle budget and on wasm32 is a comment here.

title: MCP: set WCS from feature picks

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
PR #706 grew the GUI's "Set WCS from features": pick edges, vertices, faces and cylinder walls, say which axis each one sets, and the WCS lands on the fitted frame, undoable (#701). The MCP surface cannot do the equivalent. `set_wcs` (`crates/app/src/mcp/setup_tools.rs`) takes only an absolute origin or a stock-bbox point plus offset, and rotation is a raw unit quaternion - so an agent has to solve the frame maths itself from `list_features` output, and a wrong quaternion posts shifted toolpaths with no diagnostic.

The id-driven precedent already exists: `locate_part` mates part/fixture features **by `list_features` id** and fits the 3-2-1 itself; `set_operation_geometry` takes the same ids.

**Proposal:** a tool (say `set_wcs_from_features`) taking the active setup and picks as `[{id, role}]` with `role` in `origin | x | y | z`, and:

- runs the GUI's exact law - `pick::roles::align_roles` (`crates/app/src/pick/roles.rs`): Z, X, Y priority, first axis exact, second projected perpendicular, third derived to close the frame; origin anchored at the feature's natural centre; cylinder walls by covariance fit. No second frame law to drift;
- returns refusals as MCP error strings, the same named ones the GUI says: too few picks, duplicate role, fewer than two axes, parallel axes (5 degree tilt rule), zero-length edge, unresolvable datum, stale feature id;
- queues the existing `CommandKind::SetWcs` - no new command kind, one undoable step. The "commands ship with an MCP tool" rule is satisfied by the tool itself (as noted on #706).

Filed at the reviewer's suggestion in the #706 review (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/706): keep the agent surface level with the GUI. Related: #701, #709.

title: AGENTS.md: rules for test placement, crate-to-crate dependencies and what belongs in app

labels.name: enhancement

labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
Maintainer direction (2026-11-11): high cohesion, low coupling, because every gate is costly. Put the three rules proposed in the #919 research into AGENTS.md "Code shape" and "Testing" (which still calls `crates/app/tests/` "app + commands"), and name them in the PR-reviewer checklist and the work-issue skill:

1. A test lives with the code it tests: a new test file goes in the lowest crate that provides everything it imports; its Gate map names the real crate.
2. No new dependency between our crates without a decision entry that lists the imported items, why the caller cannot pass the value in, and what now rebuilds.
3. `app` holds the document, nothing else: new code goes in `crates/app/src` only if it reads or writes the ECS world, the project file, a command, MCP or the CLI.

The fourth proposed rule (a new test joins an existing suite) is NOT part of this issue: it waits for directory suites in xtask and for timings. The exact wording of rule 2's small-dependency clause ("fewer than five items") is the maintainer's to confirm on the PR.

This issue (first step, bench only - the app's import path does not change):
1. In `crates/kernel` only: depend on the solidcore workspace crates at ONE pinned upstream commit (`rev = "<full sha>"`, never a branch). 3. A dual-importer agreement bench against truck-stepio over every STEP file under `testdata/models/` (and the fuzz / corrupt corpus): per file, both import, or one refuses by name; where both import: solid count, bounding box, volume and area agree within a stated tolerance, units agree (mm, inch, metre files - #306, #689), and the empty-parameter-list file of #887 imports. Not in this issue: switching `crates/app`'s import to solidcore, removing truck or ruststep (next issue).

body:
Maintainer decision (2026-11-11, in chat, on #901): "the units should come from a 'global setup' rather than a localized setup with operations or the machine settings.. all machines can handle mm and inch and degrees and radians.. just a matter of post output.. that setting should come from a global setting for the document rather than machine or post."

Today: the posted unit comes from the machine file (`kinematics.default.units.length` -> `machine.units`), and only the three Tormach posts read it. The document's Units choice (`SetUnits`, a radio on the Stock page) is display-only. So the user cannot find where the program's unit is set, and most posts cannot post inch at all.

Wanted:
- One document-level setting decides the unit of the posted program for every post. Recommended: the document's existing Units choice (`SetUnits`, already saved in the project file and already an undoable command with history) becomes the program unit too - one setting, not two. A second, separate derivation anywhere (machine file, post option, setup, operation) is a bug.
- The machine file's `units.length` only says which unit the file's own numbers are written in (the parser already scales them to mm); it no longer chooses the program unit. The Tormach posts switch from `machine.units` to the document's unit.
- Every post writes the program in the document's unit: inch = lengths / 25.4 at four decimals, feeds and other length-bearing words converted, and the dialect's unit word (G20 / G21, Heidenhain G70 / G71, Sinumerik G70 / G71 or G700 / G710) in the opening block. A post whose control cannot run a unit (Carvera's firmware halts on G20) refuses that document by name instead.
- The setting lives where a user looks for a document-wide choice (not only on the Stock page), and the post dialog states the unit the program will be written in.
- MCP: the existing units tool (or a new one, `area:mcp`) covers it; `EndUnits` (#596) keeps working against the document's unit.

Open point for the maintainer: angles. Every post writes rotary words in degrees today and nothing in the document chooses an angle unit. If a document-level angle unit (degrees / radians) is wanted for display or output, say so and it is filed as its own issue; it is not part of this one.

Depends on #901 (each post states the unit it writes) - land that first.

Done means: with the document set to inch, each shipped post either writes a correct inch program with its unit word (golden per post, numbers checked against the mm golden / 25.4) or refuses by name; with it set to mm, output is unchanged apart from #901's unit word; no post reads `machine.units` for the program unit; the setting is reachable at document level in the UI and through MCP.

title: Build cycle: every worktree compiles the whole dependency tree cold - share a compile cache, cut debug info, use a faster linker

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
Raised by the maintainer (2026-11-11): "why are we cold building complete bundles .. the tests are localized to crates".

## What happens today (measured on the dev machine)
- Every issue worker, reviewer and gate works in its own worktree with its own `target/`. A fresh one compiles the WHOLE dependency tree before the first test runs: about 15-25 minutes per review and 25-75 minutes per gate, almost all of it third-party crates (flecs' C through bindgen/cc, wgpu/egui, the B-rep kernel, the script engine ...), not our code.
- `Cargo.toml` sets `[profile.dev.package."*"] opt-level = 2`: every dependency is optimised in dev builds. That makes tests run faster but makes each cold build much slower.
- Nothing sets `debug`, so dev builds carry full debug info for all crates: one `target/` reaches 50-120 GB (the disk filled twice today) and every link is slow.
- Integration tests are one binary per file: `crates/app/tests` has 266 files, motion 65, sim 50. The batch gate's app step takes about 24 of its 38 minutes, much of it linking and starting 266 binaries.
- `.cargo/config.toml` holds only the `xtask` alias: no linker choice, no cache wrapper. `sccache` is not installed; `rust-lld` is.

## Wanted (this issue: the three cheap ones, measured)
1. **A shared compile cache across worktrees** (`sccache` as `RUSTC_WRAPPER`, and as the C compiler wrapper for the cc-built C code if that works on MSVC). Registry crates live at the same path for every worktree, so their compilations are cache hits; a fresh worktree should then compile only our own crates. It must be OPTIONAL: a machine without sccache builds exactly as today (enable it from `cargo xtask` / the gate wrappers when `sccache` is on PATH, or document the env var - never hard-code a wrapper in `.cargo/config.toml` that breaks a machine without it). Say how to install it and how big its cache is allowed to grow.
2. **Less debug info**: `debug = false` (or `"line-tables-only"`) for dependencies, and line tables only for our crates in dev/test - enough for backtraces and panics with file:line. Report target size and link time before/after.
3. **A faster linker** for the Windows MSVC target (`rust-lld` / `lld-link`), and the equivalent on Linux/macOS where it helps, again without breaking a machine that lacks it.
4. Re-examine `opt-level = 2` for all dependencies: keep it only for the crates whose speed the tests need (measure: batch gate time with opt-level 2 everywhere vs 1 vs a short list).

Measure and report, on the same machine, cold (empty target, warm cache where a cache applies) and warm: `cargo test -p camcraft-app --no-run`, `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test <one binary>`, `cargo xtask gate quick` on a one-file app change, and the `target/` size. No test may change behaviour; the gates stay green.

## Not in this issue (file separately if the numbers say so)
- Folding the 266 one-file app test binaries into a few binaries (one per area, files as modules). This is the biggest structural win for the gate, but it changes the gate maps in `xtask` and every "run this binary" instruction.

## Process
`.cargo/config.toml`, `xtask/` and the gate wrappers are process files: bump `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`, and say in the PR what a fork must do.

Done means: a fresh worktree reaches its first app test at least 3x faster than today with the cache warm, `target/` is at most half today's size, the settings are optional per machine and documented, and the measured numbers are in the PR.

body:
Tool library import can't update or replace tools; it only adds or renames them.

**Where:** `ImportTools` (`crates/app/src/commands/tool_import.rs:81-86`) skips an identical tool and RENAMES a same-named different one (`A (2)`). There's no replace or update mode, and no key but the name.

**Effect:** re-importing an updated library (e.g. after a feeds-and-speeds revision) adds a renamed duplicate of every changed tool, instead of updating them. *Guess:* that's every tool in a library-wide feeds change.

**Fix sketch:** an import mode with three options: add (today's behaviour), update matching tools, or replace. Matching is by name, or by part number once tools carry one (see the tool-metadata issue filed alongside this). It's one undoable command, with a preview of what changes. Add it to MCP too.

Effort: medium.

**Done means:** re-importing a revised library updates matching tools in place, with one undo; pinned.

There's no thread-mill tool kind.

- A thread-milling operation: helical interpolation, internal and external, climb or conventional, single or multi pass, radial passes.
- Simulation and gouge laws for the form.

Effort: max (a new kind, a helical op and the sim).

body:
Turning has no cutting-data model: no surface speed (Vc, m/min or SFM) or feed per revolution.

**Where:** `crates/tools/src/cutting.rs` `TABLE` holds milling windows only, and `tabulated()` (`crates/app/src/cutting.rs:41`) excludes every lathe kind. **Effect:** a lathe or mill-turn tool library has to carry placeholder values. Users enter turning data by hand per operation, with no suggestion. The posted program's S/F words (and G96/G95 where the post supports them, cf. #772) can't come from the tool.

**Fix sketch:**
- Turning rows in the cutting table: Vc and f/rev per work material, for HSS and carbide, as conservative handbook-range starting values like the milling rows.
- Lathe tools store Vc + f/rev, with a max-rpm clamp.
- Operations derive S/F, or G96/G95 on posts that state CSS.
- Old files load unchanged.

Effort: high, since it changes posted S/F words.

**Done means:** a turning op on a known material gets a suggested Vc and f/rev; posted S/F (or G96/G95) match; pinned on a lathe post golden.

body:
A tool library file (`.camtools`) can't carry a tool's drawn holder body.

**Where:** `parse_tool_library` (`crates/app/src/tool_library.rs:109`) goes through `project::tool_from_json` and `ToolDto::to_tool` (`crates/app/src/project/file.rs:462`). It returns a `Tool`, which has no body field (`crates/tools/src/tools.rs:137`), and export writes `body: None` (`file.rs:456`). A library tool can only carry the `holder_d`/`holder_len` cylinder.

That over-reports: an ER20 nut of Ø35 under a Ø46 flange reads as Ø46 all the way down. It's safe, but it gives false hits near walls, and the user must re-pick every tool's holder by hand.

**Fix:** let `.camtools` entries carry the tool body (the drawn holder profile and the built-in holder's name), round-tripped exactly like a `.camproj` tool. An older file without it still loads.

**Done means:** export then import of a tool with a built-in holder keeps its profile bit-identical; pinned.

title: Posts: a combined linear + C move is posted at the mill feed with no cap from the machine's stated C rate (fanuc.cps, doosan-dnm.cps)

labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found during the review of PR #860 (#33, C unwind), where the lathe post got this cap.

**What happens:** `assets/posts/fanuc.cps` (about lines 109-114) and `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps` (about line 287) write a C word on a combined linear + rotary move at the operation's F, with no check against the rotary rate the machine file states. A short linear move with a large C change can therefore command the rotary far faster than its stated maximum.

**What #860 does for the lathe post:** `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` (`liveMove`) caps F on every C block so that the linear part does not exceed the machine's stated linear feed and the C part does not exceed its stated C rate (deg/min; the rotary `speeds` are passed to the script by `crates/post/src/post/machine.rs`), with zero-length guards. Where the machine file states no C rate, C is uncapped by data.

**Expected:** every post that writes a rotary word on a combined move applies the same rule from the same machine data (one helper, not a copy per post), or refuses by name where it cannot. Check the other dialects that can emit A/B/C on a combined move as well (tormach.cps for the microARC A, the 5-axis posts).

**Open question for the fix:** how each control reads F on a combined move (linear feed with the rotary carried along, a combined rate, or inverse time G93) - the cap must match the feed mode the post declares; cite the control's public documentation per dialect.

Done means: no posted block can command a rotary above its stated rate or a linear axis above the stated feed; pinned per dialect by a test that reads every posted block back; existing goldens move only where a block was over the limit, each listed.

Safety floor (posted G-code): effort high, high-tier review.

**Why it matters:** an agent driving CamCraft through MCP chooses faces by `facing` for side-dependent work - `locate_part` mates, `lay_part_on_points`, work-offset picks, op geometry. A bottom face reported as "up" can put a part on the wrong side with no refusal.

**To find out first:** whether the fixture's STL has its bottom cap wound upward (then the fixture is wrong and a test with a correctly wound model must show "down"), or `facing()` does not take the normal from the facet winding / takes its absolute value (then the tool is wrong). Check with a model whose winding is known to be right (a box from the test helpers, and an imported STEP).

Done means: for a closed solid with correct winding, a downward-facing flat face reads "down" in every MCP tool that reports `facing`, pinned by a test with a cylinder and a box; if the fixture's winding was the cause, the fixture is fixed and the height-only `flat_face` helper in `mcp_pick.rs` can go back to using `facing`.

title: Adaptive growth planner: the ring opening is quadratic in outline vertices - one level of the user's STEP bore grows for ~200 s

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found while reworking #850 (PR #865).

**What happens:** app `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` (heavy lane, `testdata/models/Milling-test.step`). On main, one level's growth plan spends **~200 s in release** in `adaptive/grow.rs`: 33 revolutions, 157 trial steps, about 1.3 s per trial.

**Where the time goes** (local probe, release):
- 99 % of it is `rings::open`, the morphological opening: two `offset_fine` calls at `ARC_TOL` 2.5e-4 mm per trial, plus one per revolution for `whole`.
- The stock walk takes 0.6 s.
- The cleared-area offset and the intersect take 0.2 s each.

The opening's cost grows about with the **square** of the ring's vertex count. Measured cost per (vertices per trial)^2:

| fixture | vertices per trial | ns per (vertices)^2 |
|---|---|---|
| 60 x 14 slot | ~290 | ~63 |
| 60 x 40 island | ~700 | ~105 |
| the bore (fine STEP tessellation) | ~4,700 | ~58 |

So a finely tessellated outline turns a 33-revolution plan into minutes.

**Why it is not bounded:** #850's budget cannot refuse it without changing a plan that finishes on main. Measured on any time-faithful unit, the bore is the most expensive plan of all, so it stays law 2's (length) alone. See `docs/decisions/850-adaptive-geometry-budget.md`.

**Options:**
- Simplify the cleared area and the ring to the planner's working tolerance before the opening. Douglas-Peucker at the `MERGE` / `ARC_TOL` scale would remove the boolean engine's arc-tolerance vertices that say nothing about the shape.
- An opening that does not re-tessellate every convex vertex at `ARC_TOL`.
- An incremental opening.

Each option changes toolpaths: under the safety floor, with every adaptive fixture re-measured.

**Done means:** the bore's growth level plans in seconds (stated bound, release and debug) with the load, crossing and kink laws held. Every adaptive fixture's change is measured and named in the PR.

Related: #850, #44, #845.

title: Coolant: the machine editor drops an added Air M7, the Carvera post emits M8 from the seeded Flood, and operations can't ask for air

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
From the same Makera Z1 user report (2026-11-11). Makera machines cool with **air, M7**. The user built a Z1 machine file in the editor and tried to add M7 air cooling: **"this was ignored when I saved the profile"**. They asked to be able to:
- disable the default (flood) cooling in the editor and swap it for air; or
- keep both in the profile and choose one per operation.

**What we know from the code (main):**
- A new machine draft is seeded with `"coolants": [{ "name": "Flood", "mCode": "M8" }]` (`crates/app/src/machine/draft.rs:91`).
- `add_coolant` adds a name with **no code** (`draft.rs:147-165`). A coolant whose code is never filled in may then be skipped or dropped. That's likely the "ignored on save".
- `carvera.cps` `coolantCode()` returns the **first `Flood` entry**, else the first entry with a code. So a profile still holding the seeded Flood M8 posts **M8**, even after an Air M7 is added. On a Makera that's the wrong M-code: M8 isn't the air blast.
- Operations choose `CoolantMode` Off / Flood / Mist / Through tool (`crates/post/src/post/coolant.rs`). There's no **Air** mode, and Flood is the silent default, so an op can't ask for "air" by name. The generic posts look the word up in the machine's list and refuse by name when it's missing.

**Fix (sketch; the worker decides the details and records them):**
1. **The editor** can remove or replace the seeded Flood entry, and an added coolant gets its code entered before it's saved. A save never silently drops a coolant; it's refused by name if one is incomplete.
2. **An `Air` coolant mode** (or "air blast", M7 on Makera), selectable per operation, which the posts resolve from the machine's list like Mist.
3. **A machine-level default coolant**, so a machine whose only coolant is air defaults new operations to Air, not Flood.
4. **`carvera.cps`** posts the coolant the operation asked for, not "first Flood". If the machine has no matching entry, it's a named refusal, never a wrong M-code.

Effort: high: it changes posted G-code (safety floor).

**Done means:**
- a machine file with only Air M7 posts M7/M9 for a default operation;
- a profile edited in the GUI keeps its Air M7 after save and reload;
- an operation asking for a coolant the machine lacks is refused by name;
- all pinned.

title: An over-budget STEP mesh is imported at reduced fidelity with only a log line - gouge verdicts on it can pass a real gouge on a convex wall

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Found in the review of PR #839 (#689).

**What happens.** `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step.rs` (`shell_facets`, the refinement loop and the `eprintln!` at about lines 188-207) refines a STEP shell toward its chord target. Since #689 that target is `min(extent/1000, 0.005 mm)`. Refinement stops early once the mesh passes `budget / 8` facets (`MAX_FACETS` = 30 M, less what earlier shells used), or when a pass returns `TooLarge`. The importer then keeps the coarser mesh and only prints "step: tessellated at reduced fidelity ..." to stderr. Nothing in the model, the UI, MCP or the program gate records that the mesh is coarser than the gouge verdict assumes.

A related wrinkle: on the `Err(TooLarge) => break` path, `tol` has already been halved while `refined` is the previous, coarser mesh. The log then under-reports the chord error, and if the halved `tol` reaches the target, it says nothing at all.

**Why it matters, in both directions.** The gouge laws judge the program against these facets with a 0.01 mm verdict. A facet is a chord inscribed in the true surface, so it stands inside the material by its sagitta. That cuts both ways:

- **Concave wall** (a bore or a pocket wall): the facets stand toward the tool. A nominal finish reads as a false gouge, which is the safe side. This was the #689 symptom.
- **Convex wall** (a boss or an outside profile): the facets stand away from the tool, so the mesh wall looks farther off than the real wall. A real gouge up to the mesh's actual chord error can pass the verdict. This is the unsafe side.

AGENTS.md, Prime Directive: "if an operation can only be partly computed, mark it 'incomplete' rather than emit a subtly wrong toolpath", and "Log diagnostics, never silence". A stderr line the user never sees is silence.

This risk is not new. Before #689 every STEP mesh was made at `extent/1000`, which is never finer than what an over-budget model gets now. #689 removes the risk for every model that fits the budget. For an over-budget model it remains.

**Options.**
- (a) The import records the chord error it actually achieved on the model, and the gouge laws tighten their floor by the excess over the 0.005 mm cap for that model. That is stricter, never looser; false gouges on concave walls are the safe side.
- (b) The model is flagged "reduced fidelity" visibly in the UI and MCP. The program gate refuses to post operations judged against it until the user acknowledges it or re-imports with a larger budget.
- (c) Both.

**Recommended: (c).** (a) alone keeps the verdict sound but leaves the user wondering about false gouges. (b) alone relies on an acknowledgement.

Done means: an over-budget import is visible to the user and to MCP; no gouge verdict on such a model can be looser than on a full-fidelity one; and tests pin both, including the `TooLarge`-break path's reported chord error.

Found while working #93 (slice 2: the drawn cutter, neck and shank in the tool editor).

What happens: a milling tool's own shape can now be drawn as a spun half-outline (`schema::ToolCutter`, set by `SetToolCutter`, `camcraft_tools::cutter_profile`). By design it is display only: the generators, the stock simulation and the reach / shank / holder laws keep reading the tool's numbers (`diameter`, `flute_len`, `shank_d`, `shank_len`). The drawn outline is held to agree with those numbers (`cutter_profile::check`: exact diameter within the flutes, flute + shank length, never wider than the stated shank above the flutes), so the numbers are always the conservative envelope - but a necked tool (a reduced neck under the flutes, the whole point of buying one) is still judged as the full shank cylinder, so reach checks over-report and refuse cuts the real tool makes.

What should: the simulation's tool body and the reach laws may read the drawn outline where it is narrower than the numbers' cylinder, never where it would be wider - one source for the judged envelope, the same way the drawn holder feeds `tool_body` / the band stack.

Evidence: `crates/app/src/tool_cutter.rs` (reader/writer), `crates/tools/src/cutter_profile.rs` (agreement law); the judged envelope lives in `tool_body` / `HolderStack` and (open) PR #837 / #843 `sim_tool_body`, band stack - this must build on those once merged, not beside them.

title: adaptive growth: the overload fallback picks the largest step on truncated readings and walks it far past the bound

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
What happens: `Planner::step_search` (crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/grow.rs) tries up to 7 growth steps with `walk_until(.., limit = bound)`, which stops at the FIRST reading past the bound. When no step holds, the fallback keeps "the least overload" from those truncated readings. Where the overload sits before the g-dependent front (it does not grow with the step), every try reads the same, the tie goes to the first (largest) step, and that step is then walked whole - far past the reading it was chosen on.

Evidence (release, `HSM_ONE=island hsm_one`, island 60x40/12x12, on d1920031 with the #844 compile break stubbed locally and the growth budget lifted to reach the growth): round the island's NE corner, revs 153-159 read the same first exceedance at every step from 1.88 down to 0.088 mm (e.g. rev 159: 59.5 deg x7), the largest step was kept and walked whole at 57.5 -> 125 deg (79.4 % D at (43.66, 25.81)). This is the 125 deg / 176 breaks round 9 of #7 blamed on the spiral's geometry.

Held fix: branch `issue/7-r10-corner-reading`, e4039ef0 - re-walk each tried step whole and keep the least. Island readings with it: every overloaded revolution reads <= 55 deg (bound ~47.5; worst now at the SW wall, (17.58, 6.01)), the NE-corner overloads are gone. Cost: the growth work on the island doubles (61,971 r, vs ~31,000 before, vs the #13 `WORK_MAX` 30,000), because the smaller steps take more revolutions, and each overloaded revolution adds up to 7 whole walks.

Done means: the fallback chooses the least overload by whole readings (a pinning test where the truncated reading ties and the whole reading does not), with the #13 growth budget kept honest (either the extra walks are not charged as growth work, the re-walk is bounded, or WORK_MAX is recalibrated on the fixtures with the band refusal re-timed); goldens that move are listed.

Found while working #7 (round 10). Part of the #7 picture, but a defect on any growth plan with an overloaded revolution.

title: Synthetos TinyG post processor (3-axis mill)

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
### What are you trying to do

Post 3-axis milling programs for machines running [Synthetos TinyG](https://github.com/synthetos/TinyG) (the TinyG v8 board, ATxmega192A3), the other grbl-family hobby controller. CamCraft has no TinyG post; #710's grblHAL post is the closest, but TinyG understands a smaller set again: no canned cycles at all (G81-G89 are rejected), no G41/G42, no G84, `M6` only records the tool, tool numbers stop at 31, and the serial input acts on `!`, `~` and `%` wherever they stand in a line.

The firmware's `edge-next` branch (build 450.03) is what I maintain and test on real boards, so posted programs can be checked against its own parser and planner off the board, and on a board after that.

### How you imagine it working

A new `assets/posts/tinyg.cps` (3-axis mill), structured like `grblhal.cps` and specced from TinyG's public wiki ("Gcode Support", "Homing and Limits", "Flow Control and Footers", "Inch and Millimeter Units Mode") and the LinuxCNC G-code reference TinyG states it follows (behaviour only; the firmware source is GPL and is not read for this), plus a generic `assets/machines/tinyg-3axis.mch`.

What the post respects (each checked against the wiki and by replaying the output through the edge-next parser and planner):
- **Drilling as plain moves**: a CYCLE record writes nothing; the hole's expanded chain posts, with the dwell as `G4 P<seconds>` at the hole bottom. Tapping is refused by name (no G84, no spindle sync).
- **Tool change**: Z lift, then `T<n> M6` alone on its line, then `M0` on the next - M6 moves nothing on TinyG, so the stop is the operator's change. Tools T1-T31; a larger number is refused by name.
- **Header `G21|G20 G17 G90 G91.1 G94 G64`**: the words M30 does not reset on TinyG. No `%`, O word or N numbers; no tool length word (G43.1/G49 belong to the operator or sender, as #710 decided for grblHAL).
- **Z lift as grblHAL's**: `G53 G0 Z<safe_retract>` only when the machine file states it; otherwise the work-offset clearance, refused by name when unknown or not above the stock. No G28/G30.
- **Comments** drop `!` (feed hold), `~` (cycle start), `%` (queue flush) and the other characters the serial input acts on; lines stay under 191 bytes.
- Refused by name: control/wear compensation, going home, tilted moves; probing is refused by the engine (no parameters or expressions on TinyG).

**Done means:** `tinyg.cps` and the machine file ship in `assets/`; the post is in the conformance list (tap refused), `EXTENSIONS` and the cross-post tests like `grblhal`; a `tinyg_post` test and goldens under `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tinyg/` cover contour, pocket, face, slot, trace, drill, peck and tool change; every golden replays through the edge-next firmware's parser and planner with no refused line.

Related: #710 (grblHAL post; this stacks on #715, which it extends the same lists as), #714.

Filed from a fork, which cannot set labels. Suggested labels: enhancement, P2, area:post.

body:
Found in the high-tier review of PR #815 (#813): https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/815#pullrequestreview-5856868422

**The gap:**
- A work-turning rotary about **Y** (a table B: vector `[0,1,0]`, or none and named B) is treated as off X. It gets **no swing check, no refusal and no load note**, so a `G0 B..` index could swing the work into the retracted tool unjudged.
- It's the same risk as the A case (#804/#810, #813/#815): a vertical tool tip at height h is at least h from any horizontal line through the WCS origin.
- A rotary named A whose *stated* vector is off X falls through the same way.
- **C is safe:** turning about a vertical line keeps every point's height.

**Today it's latent:** no shipped machine has a work-turning B (millturn's C carries the head), and nothing judged any swing before #804.

**Expected:**

Split from #131 (Support Tormach machines). PR #162 noted it as a possible follow-up: "G84 on non-MX machines: non-MX 770s (R8 spindle) may not rigid-tap. Telling those machines apart needs a capability flag in the machine file."

**What happens today:** the Tormach PathPilot post writes `G84` rigid tapping for any Tormach machine file. On a machine whose spindle can't rigid-tap (an R8 non-MX 770 without the needed spindle feedback), the program would be wrong for that machine, with no warning.

**Expected:**

**Sources:** Tormach's public manuals for which models and spindles support rigid tapping. Behaviour only, per the Clean-Room Protocol. The 770MX manual (UM10587) chapter 10 covers G84 on the MX.

**Done means:**
- The capability is in the `.mch` schema, validated and shown in the Machines pane.
- Every Tormach machine file states it correctly, from the manuals.
- A Tap op on a non-capable machine is refused by name, pinned by a test.
- The 770MX G84 golden is unchanged.
